Quamvis autem testimonio principis Apostolorum de Christo, non sit, absolute loquendo, firmius ac magis authenticum testimonium David prophetæ, aut cujuslibet in veteri Testamento, sed magis econtra (quoniam gloriosi Apostoli magis illuminati fuerunt de Christo quam Prophetæ veteris Testamenti, et majori gratia erant repleti, Christi quoque mysteria clarius conspexerunt multipliciusque noverunt quam vates Mosaicæ legis : propter quod præferuntur Prophetis in sapientia, virtute, fructuositate, sanctitate, miraculis, gratia et gloria); nihilo minus quantum ad aliquos, firmius fuit testimonium David de Christo, quam testimonium beatissimi Petri, scilicet quantum ad Judæos et cavillatores, qui dicere potuerunt quod Petrus magistrum suum zelo immoderato prædicare conatus est, et ea quæ narrat, vel ficta sunt, vel in secreto audita, ideo minus credibilia quam David prophetæ oracula, quum tamen sanctissimus Petrus per plura et eminentiora miracula ostenderit, se esse locutum ex Spiritu Sancto, quam David.
paras.en: Next he proves the divinity of Christ by the irrefutable testimony of prophecy. [[1:19|And we have the more firm|Et habemus firmiorem]], that is, very firm, [[1:19|prophetical word|propheticum sermonem]], that is, the testimony of King David to the divinity of Christ, in the psalm where the Son speaks: [[Ps 2:7|The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee|Dominus dixit ad me : Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te]]. Nay, David speaks of it in several psalms, as in that: [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]; and: [[Ps 44:2|My heart hath uttered a good word|Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum]] [taken of the Word, the Son uttered by the Father]. Now although, absolutely speaking, the testimony of David the prophet, or of anyone in the Old Testament, is not firmer or more authoritative than the testimony of the prince of the Apostles about Christ, but rather the contrary (since the glorious Apostles were more enlightened about Christ than the Prophets of the Old Testament, and were filled with greater grace, and saw the mysteries of Christ more clearly and knew them in more ways than the seers of the Mosaic law: for which reason they are set above the Prophets in wisdom, virtue, fruitfulness, holiness, miracles, grace and glory); nevertheless, with respect to some, the testimony of David about Christ was firmer than the testimony of the most blessed Peter: namely with respect to the Jews and cavillers, who could say that Peter strove to preach up his master out of immoderate zeal, and that the things he tells were either feigned or heard in secret, and so less credible than the oracles of David the prophet; though in fact the most holy Peter showed by more and greater miracles than David that he spoke from the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Cui benefacitis attendentes, quasi lucernæ lucenti in caliginoso loco. Ordo verborum est : Cui sermoni prophetico quasi lucernæ lucenti in caliginoso loco attendentes, et fidem adhibentes, benefacitis, quia hoc bonum ac meritorium est. Locus autem tenebrosus est mundus iste, seu genus humanum, ignorantiarum et vitiorum tenebris obfuscatum. Est autem attendendum sermoni prophetico, donec dies illucescat, id est, dies æternitatis vobis resplendeat, atque ad claram ac beatificam Dei visionem perveniatis. De quo scriptum est in Zacharia : In illa die erit Dominus unus, et nomen ejus unum. Et lucifer, id est Christus, oriatur in cordibus vestris, id est, per speciem se vobis facie ad faciem manifestet ; vel, Lucifer, id est lumen gloriæ, vobis infundatur, et cognoscatis Deum, sicut et cogniti estis ab eo. Dicitur autem Christus lucifer, quum ipse sit oriens lucis æternæ candor, et splendor gloriæ, sapientia Patris, cui lux, sapientia, ars, idea, species, pulchritudo, appropriantur.
paras.en: [[1:19|whereunto you do well to attend, as to a light that shineth in a dark place|Cui benefacitis attendentes, quasi lucernæ lucenti in caliginoso loco]]. The order of the words is: [[1:19|whereunto|Cui]], that is, to the prophetic word, [[1:19|as to a light that shineth in a dark place|quasi lucernæ lucenti in caliginoso loco]] attending, and giving faith to it, [[1:19|you do well|benefacitis]], because this is good and meritorious [the Latin sets *benefacitis*, "you do well", between *Cui* and *attendentes*; Denis puts it last]. Now the dark place is this world, or the human race, darkened by the darkness of ignorance and vice. And we must attend to the prophetic word [[1:19|until the day dawn|donec dies illucescat]], that is, until the day of eternity shines upon you and you come to the clear and beatific vision of God. Of which it is written in Zacharias: [[Zach 14:9|in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name shall be one|In illa die erit Dominus unus, et nomen ejus unum]]. [[1:19|and the day star|Et lucifer]], that is, Christ, [[1:19|arise in your hearts|oriatur in cordibus vestris]], that is, manifest himself to you by sight [*per speciem*, that is, seen as he is, no longer through faith], [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]]; or, [[1:19|the day star|Lucifer]], that is, the light of glory, be poured into you, and you know God even as you are known by him[[1 Cor 13:12||]]. Now Christ is called the day star [*lucifer*, "light-bearer", the morning star] since he, rising, is [[Wis 7:26|the brightness of eternal light|lucis æternæ candor]], and [[Heb 1:3|the brightness of his glory|splendor gloriæ]], the wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], to whom light, wisdom, art, idea, form and beauty are appropriated [that is, ascribed to the Son in particular, though common to the three Persons].

paras.t: Hoc primum intelligentes, id est in primis agnoscentes, quod omnis prophetiæ scriptura, id est omnis scriptura prophetica ; vel, ut alii textus habent, Omnis prophetia Scripturæ, id est omnis prophetia in sacra Scriptura contenta ; propria interpretatione non fit, id est, humana adinventione non patuit, nec sensu proprio Prophetarum inventa est.
paras.en: [[1:20|Understanding this first|Hoc primum intelligentes]], that is, recognizing first of all, [[1:20|That no prophecy of scripture|quod omnis prophetiæ scriptura]] [Denis's text reads *omnis prophetiæ scriptura*, "every writing of prophecy"], that is, no prophetic writing; or, as other texts have, every [[1:20|prophecy of scripture|Omnis prophetia Scripturæ]], that is, every prophecy contained in holy Scripture: no such prophecy [[1:20|is made by private interpretation|propria interpretatione non fit]], that is, it did not come to light by human invention, nor was it found out by the Prophets' own understanding.

paras.t: Non enim voluntate humana allata est aliquando prophetia, id est, Prophetæ ex propria sua libertate et potestate non habuerunt notitiam ac gratiam prophetalem, vel quod Spiritus Sanctus eorum tangeret corda : quia futurorum pure contingentium certa præcognitio, eorum quoque quæ soli Deo patescunt, et ex ejus libertate dependent, notitia, ipsi omnipotenti supersapientissimo Creatori est propria, nec aliis nisi eo revelante, patescit. Propter quod per Isaiam scriptum est : Quæ ventura sunt annuntiate nobis, et sciemus quia dii estis vos.
paras.en: [[1:21|For prophecy came not by the will of man at any time|Non enim voluntate humana allata est aliquando prophetia]], that is, the Prophets did not have prophetic knowledge and grace of their own freedom and power, nor was it in their power that the Holy Ghost should touch their hearts: because the sure foreknowledge of things purely contingent in the future, and the knowledge also of those things which lie open to God alone and depend on his freedom, is proper to the almighty and all-surpassingly wise Creator himself, and is not open to others unless he reveals it. For which reason it is written by Isaias: [[Is 41:23|Shew the things that are to come hereafter, and we shall know that ye are gods|Quæ ventura sunt annuntiate nobis, et sciemus quia dii estis vos]].

paras.t: Sed Spiritu Sancto inspirati, id est instincti et illuminati, locuti sunt sancti Dei homines, id est sancti Prophetæ vaticinati. Propter quod loquitur et Paulus : Alii per Spiritum datur gratia prophetiæ. In libro Job quoque habetur : Inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam. Dicunt item doctores, quod gratia prophetiæ dicit actum, non habitum. Idcirco in potestate Prophetarum non est, vaticinari ad libitum, aut de quibuscumque ; sed tunc, quando a Spiritu Sancto tanguntur, et de quibus ab ipso illuminantur.
paras.en: But, [[1:21|inspired by the Holy Ghost|Sed Spiritu Sancto inspirati]], that is, moved and enlightened, [[1:21|the holy men of God spoke|locuti sunt sancti Dei homines]], that is, the holy Prophets prophesied. For which reason Paul too says: [[1 Cor 12:8|To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given|Alii per Spiritum datur]] the grace of prophecy[[1 Cor 12:10||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. xii, 8; Denis joins the opening words of v. 8 to the prophecy named in v. 10]. In the book of Job too it is said: [[Job 32:8|the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding|Inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam]] [the margin gives Job xxxii, 8, 10; the words are those of v. 8]. The doctors also say that the grace of prophecy denotes an act, not a habit [that is, a gift given for the moment, not an abiding disposition]. Therefore it is not in the power of the Prophets to prophesy at will, or about whatever they please; but only then, when they are touched by the Holy Ghost, and about those things on which they are enlightened by him.

2.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : FUERUNT VERO ET PSEUDOPROPHETÆ, ETC.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: But there were also false prophets, etc.

paras.t: Postquam præcedenti capitulo gloriosus apostolici ordinis vertex moralia documenta induxit, et Dei beneficia commemoravit, nunc contra hæreticorum errores pestiferos armat et præmunit fideles. Nam ait: Fuerunt vero et pseudoprophetæ in populo veteris Testamenti. De quibus in Jeremia, Ezechiele, Michæa, aliisque locis Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, frequenter fit mentio. Et parum ante Christi prædicationem fuerunt Theodas et Judas Galilæus, de quibus in Actibus scribitur.
paras.en: Having in the preceding chapter set out moral teachings and recalled the benefits of God, the glorious head of the apostolic order now arms and forewarns the faithful against the pestilent errors of heretics. For he says: [[2:1|But there were also false prophets among the people|Fuerunt vero et pseudoprophetæ in populo]] of the Old Testament, of whom frequent mention is made in Jeremias, Ezechiel, Micheas and other places of the Scriptures of the Old Testament. And a little before the preaching of Christ there were Theodas[[Acts 5:36||]] and Judas the Galilean[[Acts 5:37||]], of whom it is written in the Acts.

paras.t: Sicut et in vobis erunt magistri mendaces, puta hæresiarchæ, qui introducent sectas perditionis, id est speciales et falsas doctrinas, hæreticas pravitates, erroneas collectiones, ad æternam damnationem tendentes: et eum qui emit eos, Dominum, id est Christum (qui non corruptibilibus auro vel argento, sed proprio sanguine eos redemit: de quo ait Vas electionis, Empti estis pretio magno), negabunt, id est, prave de ipso sentient, et non credent, nec prædicabunt eum sicut in veritate consistit, sed talem qualem eum esse confingent; superducentes sibi cele[…] perditionem, id est, festinatam damnationem, seu damnationis causam, sibi ipsis accumulantes. De talibus ait Christus: Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces. Et Paulus in Actibus: Scio, inquit, quia post discessionem meam intrabunt in vos lupi graves, non parcentes gregi; et ex vobis ipsis surgent viri loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se.
paras.en: [[2:1|even as there shall be among you lying teachers|Sicut et in vobis erunt magistri mendaces]], namely heresiarchs, [[2:1|who shall bring in sects of perdition|qui introducent sectas perditionis]], that is, private and false doctrines, heretical depravities, erroneous inferences, tending to eternal damnation; and [[2:1|the Lord who bought them|et eum qui emit eos, Dominum]], that is, Christ (who redeemed them not with [[1 Pet 1:18|corruptible things, as gold or silver|corruptibilibus auro vel argento]], but with His own blood [the margin gives 1 Pet. ii, 18; the passage is 1 Pet 1:18–19]; of whom the Vessel of election says: [[1 Cor 6:20|you are bought with a great price|Empti estis pretio magno]]), they shall [[2:1|deny|negabunt]]: that is, they will think wrongly of Him, and will not believe or preach Him as He is in truth, but such as they make Him out to be; [[2:1|bringing upon themselves swift destruction|superducentes sibi cele perditionem]], that is, heaping up for themselves a hastened damnation, or the cause of damnation. Of such Christ says: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]]. And Paul in the Acts: [[Acts 20:29|I know|Scio]], he says, [[Acts 20:29|that after my departure ravening wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock|quia post discessionem meam intrabunt in vos lupi graves, non parcentes gregi]] [Denis reads *lupi graves*, "grievous wolves", where the Vulgate has *lupi rapaces*, "ravening wolves"]; [[Acts 20:30|And of your own selves shall arise men speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them|et ex vobis ipsis surgent viri loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se]].

paras.t: Et multi sequentur eorum luxurias, id est tam corporales quam spirituales eorum fornicationes. Nam multi illorum hæresiarcharum quatenus plures sibi allicerent, concupiscentiis frena laxabant; qui etiam spiritualiter fornicando, cor suum averterunt a Deo, et animas suas dæmonum fecerunt adulteras, verbumque Dei adulteraverunt, false exponendo Scripturas: in quibus omnibus innumerabiles sibi attraxerunt perditionis discipulos. Per quos via veritatis, id est Christus, qui ait: Ego sum via, veritas et vita. Vel, via veritatis est fides catholica, sana doctrina, conversatio veraciter christiana. De qua loquitur Dominus: Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam. Unde et Isaias ait: Hæc via, ambulate in ea; et non declinetis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram. Blasphemabitur: quia et ipsi eam blasphemarunt, hæreses et schismata inducendo et suos infelices discipulos ad idem aliciendo, infidelibus quoque dando occasionem blasphemandi Christum, ejusque legem ac fidem. Videntes namque infideles turpem vitam et varias abusiones hæreticorum, putaverunt Christum talia docuisse, et omnes Christianos hujusmodi esse. Ideo Christum et ejus cultores, fidem catholicam, legemque evangelicam blasphemaverunt.
paras.en: [[2:2|And many shall follow their riotousness|Et multi sequentur eorum luxurias]], that is, their fornications, bodily as well as spiritual. For many of those heresiarchs, so as to draw more people to themselves, slackened the reins of the lusts; and by fornicating spiritually as well they turned their heart away from God, made their souls adulteresses with the demons, and adulterated the word of God by expounding the Scriptures falsely: by all which they drew to themselves countless disciples of perdition. [[2:2|Through whom the way of truth|Per quos via veritatis]], that is, Christ, who says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]. Or the way of truth is the Catholic faith, sound doctrine, a truly Christian manner of life; of which the Lord speaks: [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life|Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam]]. Hence Isaias too says: [[Is 30:21|This is the way, walk ye in it: and go not aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left|Hæc via, ambulate in ea; et non declinetis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram]]. [[2:2|Shall be evil spoken of|Blasphemabitur]] [literally "shall be blasphemed"]: for they themselves blasphemed it, by bringing in heresies and schisms and enticing their unhappy disciples to the same, and also by giving unbelievers occasion to blaspheme Christ and His law and faith. For unbelievers, seeing the shameful life and the various abuses of the heretics, thought that Christ had taught such things and that all Christians were of that kind; and therefore they blasphemed Christ and His worshippers, the Catholic faith and the law of the Gospel.

paras.t: Et in avaritia fictis verbis de vobis negotiabuntur, id est, ex cupiditate per callida et adulatoria verba vos fallent, et quasi contractum quemdam de vobis efficient, temporalia bona vestra a vobis fallaciter auferendo, non violenter, sed fraudulenter: quia ut asserit Paulus, Per benedictiones et dulces sermones decipiunt innocentium corda; et Christus, Hi sunt qui devorant domos viduarum. Itemque, hujusmodi operarii subdoli non serviunt Christo, sed suo ventri.
paras.en: [[2:3|And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you|Et in avaritia fictis verbis de vobis negotiabuntur]]: that is, out of greed they will deceive you with cunning and flattering words, and make a kind of bargain of you, taking your temporal goods from you by deceit, not by violence but by fraud. For, as Paul declares, [[Rom 16:18|by pleasing speeches and good words seduce the hearts of the innocent|Per benedictiones et dulces sermones decipiunt innocentium corda]]; and Christ: These are they [[Luke 20:47|who devour the houses of widows|qui devorant domos viduarum]]. And again, such [[2 Cor 11:13|deceitful workmen|operarii subdoli]] [[Rom 16:18|serve not Christ our Lord but their own belly|non serviunt Christo, sed suo ventri]].

paras.t: Quibus judicium jam olim non cessat, id est, reprobationis judicium dudum de eis prænuntiatum in sanctis Scripturis, non est revocatum, neque finitum, quoniam pœna eis instans ac debita, est æterna, et in perpetuum reprobati manebunt; et perditio eorum non dormitat, quia eorum damnatio non quiescet, et nunc in vita hac perditi sunt per demerita propria.
paras.en: [[2:3|Whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not|Quibus judicium jam olim non cessat]]: that is, the judgment of reprobation foretold of them long ago in the holy Scriptures has not been revoked, nor is it ended, since the punishment that awaits them and is their due is eternal, and they will remain reprobate for ever; [[2:3|and their perdition slumbereth not|et perditio eorum non dormitat]], for their damnation will not rest, and even now in this life they are lost through their own demerits.

paras.t: De his perversis hæreticisque magistris multa in B. Pauli leguntur epistolis: ut quum ait ad Galatas, Quicumque volunt placere in carne, hi cogunt vos circumcidi. De quibus et ad Timotheum multa effatur. Denique tempore Apostolorum cœperunt exsurgere, ut Paulus testatur. Inter quos fuerunt Ebion et Cerinthus, qui Christi deitatem negabant. Et Marcion, qui eum phantasticum corpus asseruit assumpsisse: cujus perfidiam postmodum auxit sacrilegus Manichæus. Arius quoque et Photinus atque Nestorius, negabant Christum esse verum Deum. Sabellius vero mentitus est eamdem personam esse Patrem et Filium et Spiritum Sanctum. Apollinaris rudissimus, negabat Christum animam habuisse rationalem. Itaque isti et eis consimiles, Christum et ejus fidem atque doctrinam blasphemaverunt.
paras.en: Of these perverse and heretical teachers much is read in the epistles of blessed Paul, as when he says to the Galatians: [[Gal 6:12|as many as desire to please in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised|Quicumque volunt placere in carne, hi cogunt vos circumcidi]]. Of them he also says much to Timothy[[2 Tim 3:1||]]. In short, they began to rise up in the time of the Apostles, as Paul bears witness. Among them were Ebion and Cerinthus, who denied the Godhead of Christ; and Marcion, who asserted that He took a phantom body, whose faithlessness the sacrilegious Manichæus afterwards increased. Arius too, and Photinus and Nestorius, denied that Christ is true God. Sabellius lyingly said that the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost are the same person. The most ignorant Apollinaris denied that Christ had a rational soul. And so these men, and others like them, blasphemed Christ and His faith and doctrine.

paras.t: Insuper, per exempla ostendit hos esse acriter puniendos. Si, pro Quia, Deus an[…] […] de quibus in libro Job habetur: In angelis suis reperit pravitatem; sed rudentibus inferni detractos in tartarum tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari. Littera hæc intricata, sic ordinanda est et exponenda: sed ipsos angelos qui peccaverunt, detractos rudentibus inferni, id est infernalibus funibus seu vinculis, quæ sunt eorum peccata, juxta quod in Proverbiis asseritur, Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur. His, inquam, funibus angelos detractos, id est deorsum projectos, et tractos a rigore divinæ justitiæ in tartarum, utpote in aerem caliginosum, qui quibusdam illorum pro carcere infernali est deputatus ad exercitium hominum; vel, In tartarum, id est infernum inferiorem sub terra situm, in quem multi projecti sunt. Illuc ergo detractos tradidit, id est, præcepit sive disposuit vel dedit, eos reservari cruciandos, quia ignem suum secum ferunt ubique, in judicium, id est usque in diem judicii: quia tamdiu reservantur hinc inde in aere sive inferius, et in die judicii graviter affligentur, ad Judicis deducti præsentiam, qui tunc eos inferno inferiori sine fine adjiciet. Tuncque augebitur pœna eorum accidentalis ex infelicium societate et condemnatione quos deceperunt, quemadmodum accidentale præmium angelorum sanctorum tunc crescet ex eorum consortio quos custodierunt. Quemadmodum ergo angelis peccantibus Dominus non pepercit, ita nec hæreticis parcet, quamvis omnes citra condignum torqueantur. Tametsi enim angeli boni et mali sint in termino, nec mereantur quantum ad essentialem felicitatem sive calamitatem, tamen quantum ad accidentale præmium seu tormentum, possunt interim mereri aut demereri.
paras.en: Further, he shows by examples that these men are to be sharply punished. [[2:4|For if|Si]], put for *since* [Latin *Si*, "if", standing for *Quia*, "since"], [[2:4|God spared not the angels that sinned|Deus an]] [some words are lost in the transcription here] […] of whom it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 4:18|in his angels he found wickedness|In angelis suis reperit pravitatem]]; [[2:4|but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower hell, unto torments, to be reserved unto judgment|sed rudentibus inferni detractos in tartarum tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari]]. This involved text is to be set in order and expounded thus: [[2:4|but|sed]] the angels themselves who sinned, [[2:4|drawn down by infernal ropes|detractos rudentibus inferni]], that is, by the cords or bonds of hell, which are their sins, according to what is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]]. Drawn down, I say, by these ropes, that is, cast downwards and dragged by the rigour of divine justice [[2:4|to the lower hell|in tartarum]] [Latin *in tartarum*, "into Tartarus"], that is, into the dark air, which has been appointed to some of them as their prison of hell, for the exercising of men; or, *into Tartarus*, that is, into the lower hell situated beneath the earth, into which many have been cast. Having drawn them down there, then, He [[2:4|delivered|tradidit]], that is, commanded, or ordained, or gave, them [[2:4|unto torments, to be reserved|reservari cruciandos]] (for they carry their fire with them everywhere) [[2:4|unto judgment|in judicium]], that is, until the day of judgment: for so long they are kept here and there in the air or below, and on the day of judgment they will be grievously afflicted, when they are brought into the presence of the Judge, who will then cast them into the lower hell without end. And then their accidental punishment will be increased by the company and condemnation of the unhappy men whom they deceived, just as the accidental reward of the holy angels will then grow by the fellowship of those whom they guarded [the "accidental" reward or pain is what is added to the essential bliss of seeing God, or to the essential pain of losing Him]. As, then, the Lord spared not the angels that sinned, so neither will He spare heretics, although all are tormented less than they deserve. For though the angels, good and bad, are at their term, and do not merit as regards essential happiness or misery, yet as regards accidental reward or torment they can meanwhile merit or demerit.

paras.t: Deinde inducit secundum exemplum, in quo evidenter terribiliterque apparuit rigor divinæ justitiæ. Et originali mundo, id est generi humano quod fuit in prima mundi ætate, puta hominibus qui ante diluvium exstiterunt, non pepercit; sed octavum Noe justitiæ præconem custodivit. In Canonica S. Judæ apostoli scriptum est: Prophetavit septimus ab Adam Enoch, etc. Posset itaque aliquis forsitan opinari, quod sicut Enoch fuit in ordine genealogiæ septimus ab Adam, sic Noe vocetur octavus quasi ab Adam octavus in ordine habeatur. Quod dici non potest, quia decimus fuit ab Adam. Siquidem in Genesi fertur, quod Enoch genuit Mathusalem, de quo natus est Lamech pater istius Noe. Dicitur ergo Noe octavus, quia inter eos qui erant in arca, fuit octavus, incipiendo numerationem ab inferiori usque ad supremum, videlicet ipsum Noe. Fuerunt namque in arca tres filii ejus cum tribus uxoribus, uxor quoque Noe et ipse. Vocatur quoque præco justitiæ, quia justitiam Dei et pœnitentiam, veritatisque viam, hominibus illius temporis denuntiavit, sicut in expositione præcedentis epistolæ patuit. Custodivit vero Deus Noe, quia a submersione diluvii eum eripuit. Diluvium mundo impiorum inducens, id est hominibus impiis tunc in mundo morantibus, qui viam suam corruperunt. Quorum tanta fuit malitia, ut in Genesi dicatur: Videns Deus quia multa malitia hominum esset in terra, et cuncta cogitatio cordis humani intenta esset ad malum omni tempore, pœnituit eum quod fecisset hominem in terra; et præcavens in futurum, tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus: Delebo, inquit, hominem quem creavi, a facie terræ. Quemadmodum ergo illis Deus non pepercit, ita nec hæreticis parcet.
paras.en: Next he brings in a second example, in which the rigour of divine justice appeared plainly and terribly. And [[2:5|the original world|Et originali mundo]], that is, the human race that existed in the first age of the world, namely the men who lived before the flood, he [[2:5|spared not|non pepercit]], [[2:5|but preserved Noe, the eighth person, the preacher of justice|sed octavum Noe justitiæ præconem custodivit]]. In the Canonical Epistle of St. Jude the apostle it is written: [[Jude 1:14|Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied|Prophetavit septimus ab Adam Enoch]], etc. Someone might therefore perhaps think that, just as Enoch was seventh from Adam in the order of the genealogy, so Noe is called the eighth as being held eighth in order from Adam. That cannot be said, since he was the tenth from Adam: for it is related in Genesis that Enoch begot Mathusala, of whom was born Lamech, the father of this Noe. Noe is therefore called the eighth because among those who were in the ark he was the eighth, beginning the count from the lowest and going up to the highest, that is, to Noe himself. For in the ark there were his three sons with their three wives, Noe's wife also, and he himself[[Gen 7:7||]]. He is also called *the preacher of justice* because he proclaimed the justice of God, and penance, and the way of truth, to the men of that time, as was shown in the exposition of the preceding epistle[[1 Pet 3:19||]][[1 Pet 3:20||]]. And God *preserved* Noe, for He rescued him from drowning in the flood. [[2:5|Bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly|Diluvium mundo impiorum inducens]], that is, upon the ungodly men then dwelling in the world, who had corrupted their way. Their wickedness was so great that it is said in Genesis: [[Gen 6:5|God seeing that the wickedness of men was great on the earth, and that all the thought of their heart was bent upon evil at all times|Videns Deus quia multa malitia hominum esset in terra, et cuncta cogitatio cordis humani intenta esset ad malum omni tempore]], [[Gen 6:6|It repented him that he had made man on the earth|pœnituit eum quod fecisset hominem in terra]]; and, taking precaution for the future [these words of Denis's text are not in the Douay-Rheims], [[Gen 6:6|being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart|tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus]]: [[Gen 6:7|I will destroy man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth|Delebo, inquit, hominem quem creavi, a facie terræ]]. As, then, God spared not them, so neither will He spare heretics.

paras.t: Deinceps exemplum tertium subditur. Et civitates Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum in cinerem redigens, id est, Sodomam et Gomorrham redegit in pulverem, quoniam ignem et sulfur abundantissime pluit super eas et habitatores, imo super totam Pentapolim: cujus civitates in Deuteronomio exprimuntur, videlicet Sodoma et Gomorrha, Adama et Seboim. Quinta urbs fuit Segor. Quibus in pulverem ex sulfureo igne redactis cum adjacentibus terris, operuit terram illam mari Mortuo, in quo nihil vivere potest. Suntque ibi arbores poma apparatu pulcherrima deferentes: quæ poma si manu tractentur, in cinerem resolvuntur, et fumum emittunt, quasi adhuc essent ardentia. Unde in Sapientiæ libro legitur: Hæc justum a pereuntibus impiis liberavit fugientem, descendente igne in Pentapolim: cujus in testimonium nequitiæ fumigabunda constat deserta terra, et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores. Eversione damnavit, id est, præfatas urbes ita evertens seu destruens, habitatores ejus sic punivit et condemnavit. Exemplum eorum qui impie acturi sunt ponens, id est, per illam combustionem et eversionem exemplariter pandens, qualiter igne æternali sunt puniendi iniqui, præsertim hæretici.
paras.en: Then a third example is added. [[2:6|And reducing the cities of the Sodomites and of the Gomorrhites into ashes|Et civitates Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum in cinerem redigens]]: that is, He reduced Sodom and Gomorrha to dust, since He rained fire and brimstone most abundantly upon them and their inhabitants[[Gen 19:24||]][[Gen 19:25||]], indeed upon the whole Pentapolis, whose cities are named in Deuteronomy, namely Sodom and Gomorrha, Adama and Seboim[[Deut 29:23||]]; the fifth city was Segor. When these had been reduced to dust by the sulphurous fire, together with the lands lying about them, He covered that land with the Dead Sea, in which nothing can live. And there are trees there bearing apples most beautiful to look at, which, if they are handled, crumble into ashes and give off smoke, as though they were still burning. Hence we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 10:6|She delivered the just man, who fled from the wicked that were perishing, when the fire came down upon Pentapolis|Hæc justum a pereuntibus impiis liberavit fugientem, descendente igne in Pentapolim]]: [[Wis 10:7|Whose land, for a testimony of their wickedness, is desolate, and smoketh to this day, and the trees bear fruits that ripen not|cujus in testimonium nequitiæ fumigabunda constat deserta terra, et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores]] [literally "trees bearing fruit at no certain season"]. [[2:6|Condemned them to be overthrown|Eversione damnavit]]: that is, by overturning or destroying the said cities in this way He so punished and condemned their inhabitants. [[2:6|Making them an example to those that should after act wickedly|Exemplum eorum qui impie acturi sunt ponens]]: that is, showing by way of example, through that burning and overthrow, how the wicked, especially heretics, are to be punished with eternal fire.

paras.t: Et justum Lot: cujus justitiam innuit Paulus ad Hebræos: Hospitalitatem, inquiens, nolite oblivisci; per hanc enim placuerunt quidam (videlicet Abraham et Lot) angelis hospitio susceptis (ut patet in Genesi): a nefandorum injuria, id est violentia, et luxuriosa conversatione eripuit, id est, a turpissimis Sodomitarum inquinamentis præservavit, atque per angelos ex Sodoma duxit. Et recte Sodomitæ, qui vitiis contra naturam sordebant, vocantur nefandi, tanquam penitus detestabiles et inhumani. Qui verbis et factis injuriam intulerunt beato Lot, juxta illud Genesis: Ingressus es, inquiunt, ut advena, numquid ut judices? Te ipsum ergo magis quam hos affligemus. Vimque faciebant Lot vehementissime.
paras.en: And [[2:7|just Lot|Et justum Lot]], whose justice Paul hints at to the Hebrews, saying: [[Heb 13:2|hospitality|Hospitalitatem]], [[Heb 13:2|do not forget: for by this some|nolite oblivisci; per hanc enim placuerunt quidam]] [Denis reads *placuerunt*, "some have pleased", where the Vulgate has *latuerunt*, "some, being not aware of it"] (namely Abraham and Lot) [[Heb 13:2|have entertained angels|angelis hospitio susceptis]] (as appears in Genesis[[Gen 18:1||]][[Gen 19:1||]]): from [[2:7|the injustice|a nefandorum injuria]] of the wicked, that is, from their violence, [[2:7|and lewd conversation|et luxuriosa conversatione]] he [[2:7|delivered|eripuit]] him: that is, He kept him from the most shameful defilements of the Sodomites and led him out of Sodom by the angels[[Gen 19:1||]]. And the Sodomites, who were befouled with vices against nature, are rightly called *nefandi* [that is, "unspeakable", "abominable"; the Douay-Rheims has "the wicked"], as wholly detestable and inhuman. They did injury to blessed Lot by word and deed, according to that of Genesis: [[Gen 19:9|Thou camest in, said they, as a stranger, was it to be a judge? therefore we will afflict thee more than them. And they pressed very violently upon Lot|Ingressus es, inquiunt, ut advena, numquid ut judices? Te ipsum ergo magis quam hos affligemus. Vimque faciebant Lot vehementissime]].

paras.t: Adspectu enim et auditu justus erat. Quod dupliciter potest intelligi: Primo, quod Lot tam custodite se habuit, quod nec ex visis, nec ex auditis Sodomitarum flagitiis a sua puritate et æquitate collapsus est, quum tamen dicat Scriptura: Cum perverso perverteris. Secundo, quod tam virtuose vixit, quod impii illi nihil iniquum viderunt in eo, nec perceperunt de ipso, sicut de Judith vidua fertur: Metuebat Dominum valde, nec erat qui loqueretur de ea verbum malum. De beatissimi quoque Joannis Baptistæ parentibus venerandis ac sanctis scriptum est: Incedebant in omnibus justificationibus Domini sine querela. Sic et sanctus Job de se ipso fatetur: Auris audiens beatificabat me, et oculus videns testimonium perhibuit mihi. Denique istud arduum fuit, et magnæ perfectionis indicium in Lot, quoniam teste Gregorio, inter imperfectos perfecte conversari, et inter iniquos juste se habere, est valde laudabile.
paras.en: [[2:8|For in sight and hearing he was just|Adspectu enim et auditu justus erat]]. This can be understood in two ways. First, that Lot kept such guard over himself that he did not fall from his purity and uprightness through the crimes of the Sodomites that he saw or heard, although Scripture says: [[Ps 17:27|with the perverse thou wilt be perverted|Cum perverso perverteris]]. Second, that he lived so virtuously that those ungodly men saw nothing wicked in him and learned nothing of the kind about him; as is related of the widow Judith: [[Jdt 8:8|she feared the Lord very much, neither was there any one that spoke an ill word of her|Metuebat Dominum valde, nec erat qui loqueretur de ea verbum malum]]. Of the venerable and holy parents of the most blessed John the Baptist, too, it is written: [[Luke 1:6|walking in all the commandments and justifications of the Lord without blame|Incedebant in omnibus justificationibus Domini sine querela]]. So also holy Job says of himself: [[Job 29:11|The ear that heard me blessed me, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me|Auris audiens beatificabat me, et oculus videns testimonium perhibuit mihi]]. Finally, this was a hard thing and a sign of great perfection in Lot, since, on the witness of Gregory, to live perfectly among the imperfect and to behave justly among the wicked is highly praiseworthy.

paras.t: Et quoniam justis grave est injustitiam cernere, subditur: habitans apud eos, id est Lot habitans inter Sodomitas, qui de die in diem animam justam iniquis operibus cruciabant, id est, quotidie ipsum Lot suis pravissimis afflixerunt sceleribus. Justus namque, tam ex Dei amore, quam ex proximorum dilectione atque ex zelo suæ justitiæ, de impiorum vitiis contristatur, præsertim quum ea emendare non potest; et dicere potest Domino cum Propheta: Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei.
paras.en: And since it is grievous for the just to look upon injustice, there follows: [[2:8|dwelling among them|habitans apud eos]], that is, Lot dwelling among the Sodomites, [[2:8|who from day to day vexed the just soul with unjust works|qui de die in diem animam justam iniquis operibus cruciabant]], that is, who afflicted Lot every day with their most depraved crimes. For the just man, out of love of God as much as out of charity towards his neighbours and zeal for his own justice, is grieved at the vices of the ungodly, especially when he cannot amend them; and he can say to the Lord with the Prophet: [[Ps 118:139|My zeal hath made me pine away: because my enemies forgot thy words|Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei]].

paras.t: Ex quibus concludit Archiapostolus: Novit Deus pios de tentatione eripere, id est de omni tribulatione eruere, quum dicat in Psalmo: Cum ipso sum in tribulatione, eripiam eum, et glorificabo eum. Eripit autem eos loco, modo et tempore sibi placente, et prout saluti expedit electorum. Idcirco in tribulationibus et tentationibus constituti, patienter et longanimiter ferre debent, et Dominum exorare ut eos indesinenter roboret et conservet, atque quum ei placuerit, ipsisque expedit, finem tribulationi dignetur imponere. Unde quum Ozias princeps Judæorum dixisset, quod nisi infra quinque dies veniret eis a Deo auxilium, urbem traderet in manus Assyriorum, virtuosa ac sapiens Judith dixit: Qui estis vos, qui tentatis Deum? Posuistis vos tempus miserationi Domini, et in arbitrio vestro diem constituistis ei.
paras.en: From this the Archapostle concludes: [[2:9|The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly from temptation|Novit Deus pios de tentatione eripere]] [Denis reads *Deus*, "God", for *Dominus*], that is, to rescue them from every tribulation, since He says in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione, eripiam eum, et glorificabo eum]]. He delivers them at the place, in the manner and at the time that please Him, and as is expedient for the salvation of the elect. Therefore those who are set in tribulations and temptations ought to bear them patiently and with long-suffering, and to beg the Lord to strengthen and keep them without ceasing, and, when it pleases Him and is expedient for them, to deign to put an end to the tribulation. Hence, when Ozias, the prince of the Jews, had said that unless help came to them from God within five days he would deliver the city into the hands of the Assyrians[[Jdt 7:23||]][[Jdt 7:25||]], the virtuous and wise Judith said: [[Jdt 8:11|who are you that tempt the Lord?|Qui estis vos, qui tentatis Deum?]] [[Jdt 8:13|You have set a time for the mercy of the Lord, and you have appointed him a day, according to your pleasure|Posuistis vos tempus miserationi Domini, et in arbitrio vestro diem constituistis ei]].

paras.t: Iniquos vero in diem judicii cruciandos reservare. Non est hoc ita intelligendum quasi iniqui ante diem generalis judicii non sint damnandi et cruciandi, sed quia tunc in corpore et anima damnabuntur, qui interim in die particularis sui judicii condemnantur in anima.
paras.en: [[2:9|But to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be tormented|Iniquos vero in diem judicii cruciandos reservare]]. This is not to be understood as though the wicked were not to be damned and tormented before the day of the general judgment, but that then they will be damned in body and soul, who in the meantime are condemned in the soul on the day of their own particular judgment.

paras.t: Gravissime vero punientur hæresiarchæ, sicut subjungitur. Magis autem eos reservat in judicio cruciandos, qui post carnem in concupiscentia immunditiæ ambulant, id est, carnales et fœdas concupiscentias assequuntur, dominationemque contemnunt, id est, tam Christo omnium dominatori, quam ejus vicariis, sanctis Apostolis, imo et summo Antistiti renuunt obedire; audaces, id est temerarii ac præsumptuosi, confingendo dogmata nova; sibi placentes, id est magni et sapientes in oculis suis. Quocontra ad Romanos dicitur: Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere, et non nobis placere; unusquisque proximo suo placeat in bonum, ad ædificationem: etenim Christus sibi non placuit. Et apud Isaiam ait Scriptura: Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes. Idcirco in Proverbiis Salomon loquitur: Ne sis sapiens apud temetipsum, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ.
paras.en: But the heresiarchs will be punished most heavily, as follows: [[2:10|And especially them|Magis autem eos]] He reserves to be tormented in the judgment [[2:10|who walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness|qui post carnem in concupiscentia immunditiæ ambulant]], that is, who pursue carnal and foul lusts, [[2:10|and despise government|dominationemque contemnunt]], that is, refuse to obey Christ, the Lord of all, as well as His vicars, the holy Apostles, and indeed the supreme Pontiff; [[2:10|audacious|audaces]], that is, rash and presumptuous, in making up new dogmas; [[2:10|self willed|sibi placentes]] [Latin *sibi placentes*, "pleasing themselves", the word the quotations that follow take up], that is, great and wise in their own eyes. Against this it is said to the Romans: [[Rom 15:1|we that are stronger ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves|Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere, et non nobis placere]]; [[Rom 15:2|every one of you Please his neighbour unto good, to edification|unusquisque proximo suo placeat in bonum, ad ædificationem]]: [[Rom 15:3|For Christ did not please himself|etenim Christus sibi non placuit]]. And in Isaias Scripture says: [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own conceits|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes]]. Therefore Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:7|Be not wise in thy own conceit|Ne sis sapiens apud temetipsum]], [[Prov 3:5|and lean not upon thy own prudence|et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ]].

paras.t: Sectas non metuunt introducere, id est hæreticas pravitates et schismata invenire ac spargere: quia Scripturas secundum proprium ingenium præsumunt exponere, et de sua subtilitate atque peritia stulte impiissimeque confidunt, quum Scripturæ eo spiritu sint intelligendæ quo et primum sunt revelatæ; blasphemantes (ut dictum est) Christum et ejus doctrinam.
paras.en: [[2:10|they fear not to bring in sects|Sectas non metuunt introducere]], that is, to invent and spread heretical depravities and schisms: for they presume to expound the Scriptures according to their own wit, and trust foolishly and most impiously in their own subtlety and skill, whereas the Scriptures are to be understood by the same Spirit by which they were first revealed; [[2:10|blaspheming|blasphemantes]] (as has been said) Christ and His doctrine.

paras.t: Ubi, id est, in eo quod dominationem contemnunt, et audaces sibimet placent, angeli, scilicet mali, fortitudine naturæ, et virtute potentiæ, quum sint majores hominibus, id est naturaliter altiores. Sunt enim speciei eminentioris quam homo, et per consequens naturaliter fortioris naturæ, utpote incorruptibiliores et in naturalibus viribus vigorosiores, puta intellectu et voluntate, præsertim quum (divino Dionysio testante) naturalia in dæmonibus manserint integra. Non portant, id est, sufferre vix valent, adversus se exsecrabile judicium, id est districtum Dei judicium contra eos jam datum: quod quamvis sit in se ipso justum et sanctum, tamen patientibus durum est et exsecrandum videtur. Similiter supplicium eis inflictum, exsecrabile eis est. Si ergo angelis tam potentibus ac potentioribus ipsis hominibus, tam intolerabilia sunt inflicta tormenta, sequitur quod intolerabiliora erunt impiis hæreticisque hominibus, maxime hæresiarchis, de quibus ad litteram agitur.
paras.en: [[2:11|Whereas|Ubi]], that is, in this, that they despise government and boldly please themselves, [[2:11|angels|angeli]], namely the evil ones, [[2:11|in strength|fortitudine]] of nature [[2:11|and power|et virtute]] of might, [[2:11|who are greater|quum sint majores]] than men, that is, higher by nature: for they are of a more eminent species than man, and consequently of a naturally stronger nature, being more incorruptible and more vigorous in their natural powers, namely understanding and will; especially since (on the witness of the divine Dionysius) their natural gifts have remained whole in the demons. [[2:11|bring not|Non portant]] [Denis takes *non portant* as "do not bear", and *exsecrabile* below as "execrable"], that is, can scarcely endure, [[2:11|against themselves a railing judgment|adversus se exsecrabile judicium]], that is, the strict judgment of God already given against them, which, though in itself it is just and holy, yet is hard to those who suffer it and seems to them execrable. Likewise the punishment inflicted on them is execrable to them. If, then, such intolerable torments have been inflicted on angels so mighty, and mightier than men themselves, it follows that more intolerable ones will be inflicted on ungodly and heretical men, above all on the heresiarchs, of whom the text treats literally.

paras.t: Itaque ex prædictis sequi apparet, quod major damnatio sit hæresiarcharum, quam eorum qui perierunt diluvio et Sodomitarum, imo et dæmonum, saltem quorumdam. Nam et Christus in Evangelio protestatur, quod in die judicii remissius erit terræ Sodomorum, quam civitatibus quæ prædicationem ejus non receperunt, nec per ejus miracula sunt conversæ. Per Ezechielem Dominus quoque testatur, quod Sodoma non peccavit dimidium peccatorum quæ perpetraverunt Judæi. Dæmones etiam non sunt omnes æque iniqui, quum de singulis ordinibus aliqui credantur ruisse. Et sicut homines electi ad singulos angelorum ordines assumuntur, et eis parificantur in gloria, sic probabiliter creditur quod diversi reprobi secundum suorum diversitatem ac gradum demeritorum, singulorum chororum dæmonibus coæquabuntur in pœnis. Præterea, loquendo in genere, peccata spiritualia graviora sunt peccatis carnalibus, et peccata in Deum, peccatis in proximum. Peccata autem hæresiarcharum sunt inter spiritualia vitia et inter facinora in Deum gravissima, præsertim quia et tot homines involvunt erroribus, quorum omnium peccata et tormenta redundant in hæresiarchas. Peccata autem Sodomitarum et diluvio eversorum fuerunt carnalia atque in proximum. Interim dæmones una transgressione positi fuerunt in termino, nec interim demeruerunt: sicut nec angeli sancti post primam ad Deum conversionem (qua positi fuerunt in termino) promeruerunt, loquendo de merito ac demerito quantum ad præmium essentiale, seu calamitatem principalem. Hæresiarchæ vero plurimis et quasi innumeris transgressionibus demeruerunt, et ad sui cursus terminum pervenerunt.
paras.en: And so from what has been said it appears to follow that the damnation of the heresiarchs is greater than that of those who perished in the flood and of the Sodomites, and even than that of the demons, at least of some of them. For Christ too declares in the Gospel that [[Matt 11:24|it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment|in die judicii remissius erit terræ Sodomorum]] than for the cities which did not receive His preaching and were not converted by His miracles[[Luke 10:12||]]. Through Ezechiel also the Lord bears witness that Sodom did not commit half the sins that the Jews committed[[Ezech 16:49||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xvi, 49–51; there Sodom has "not done as thou hast done" (v. 48), and it is Samaria that "committed not half thy sins" (v. 51)]. Nor are all the demons equally wicked, since some are believed to have fallen from each of the orders. And just as elect men are taken up into the several orders of the angels and made equal to them in glory, so it is believed with probability that the various reprobate, according to the diversity and degree of their demerits, will be made equal in punishment to the demons of the several choirs. Moreover, speaking in general, spiritual sins are graver than carnal sins, and sins against God than sins against one's neighbour. Now the sins of the heresiarchs are the gravest among spiritual vices and among crimes against God, especially since they also entangle so many men in errors, the sins and torments of all of whom redound upon the heresiarchs; whereas the sins of the Sodomites and of those destroyed by the flood were carnal and against their neighbour. Again, the demons were set at their term by a single transgression and have not demerited since, just as the holy angels have not merited since their first turning to God (by which they were set at their term), speaking of merit and demerit as regards the essential reward or the principal misery. But the heresiarchs demerited by very many and almost countless transgressions before they came to the end of their course.

paras.t: Hi vero hæresiarchæ qui sectas introducunt, velut irrationabilia pecora naturaliter in captionem et in perniciem, id est, sicut bruta naturaliter omni ratione carentia faciliter seducuntur, ita quod cadunt in lacum quo capiuntur et occiduntur, sic et hæretici in his quæ ignorant blasphemantes, id est, in his quæ fidei sunt, quæ non intelligunt, committunt blasphemias, Christi divinitatem, seu alias fidei veritates negando, in corruptione sua peribunt, id est, propter suos errores et excessus (per quos eorum intellectus et voluntas spiritualiter corrumpuntur, inficiuntur, necantur) condemnabuntur, percipientes mercedem injustitiæ, id est debitam punitionem suæ perversitatis.
paras.en: [[2:12|But these men|Hi vero]], the heresiarchs who bring in sects, [[2:12|as irrational beasts, naturally tending to the snare and to destruction|velut irrationabilia pecora naturaliter in captionem et in perniciem]]: that is, as brute beasts, by nature lacking all reason, are easily led astray, so that they fall into the pit in which they are caught and killed, so too the heretics, [[2:12|blaspheming those things which they know not|in his quæ ignorant blasphemantes]], that is, committing blasphemies in the things of faith which they do not understand, by denying the Godhead of Christ or other truths of the faith, [[2:12|shall perish in their corruption|in corruptione sua peribunt]], that is, they will be condemned for their errors and excesses (by which their understanding and will are spiritually corrupted, infected and slain), [[2:13|Receiving the reward of their injustice|percipientes mercedem injustitiæ]], that is, the punishment due to their perversity.

paras.t: Voluptatem existimantes diei delicias coinquinationis et maculæ, id est, hæretici isti in tantum obtenebrantur, quod delicias coinquinationis et maculæ, id est, delectationes carnales, fœdas, venereas, præsertim ad tactum et gustum pertinentes, reputant esse voluptatem diei, id est tam licitas et honestas, quasi alia et melior voluptas haberi non possit in die. Sicque per voluptatem diei designatur voluptas licita et sincera.
paras.en: [[2:13|counting for a pleasure the delights of a day|Voluptatem existimantes diei delicias]] [[2:13|stains and spots|coinquinationis et maculæ]] [Denis reads *coinquinationis et maculæ*, "of defilement and stain", where the Vulgate has *coinquinationes et maculæ*, "stains and spots"; and he takes *diei*, "of the day", with *voluptatem*: "counting the delights of defilement and stain a pleasure of the day"]: that is, these heretics are so darkened that they reckon the delights of defilement and stain, that is, carnal, foul and venereal pleasures, especially those belonging to touch and taste, to be a pleasure of the day, that is, so lawful and honourable that no other and better pleasure could be had in the day. And so by *the pleasure of the day* is meant a lawful and pure pleasure.

paras.t: Quemadmodum enim duplex est concupiscentia, utpote carnalis et inordinata, et spiritualis ac ordinata, ut dictum est, sic duplex est voluptas, vel delectatio sequens eam. Voluptas bona et licita, est delectatio actui virtuoso annexa. Quælibet etenim virtus propriam habet delectationem operationi suæ conjunctam, quemadmodum in Proverbiis scriptum est: Gaudium est justo facere justitiam. Et Aristoteles ait: Signum virtutis est delectatio contingens in opere. De hac voluptate ait Propheta: Delectasti me, Domine, in factura tua; et, Torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos. Voluptas prava et vitiosa est omnis delectatio actui illicito juncta. De qua in Ecclesiaste asseritur: Adolescentia et voluptas vana sunt; et in Ecclesiastico, Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluptate tua avertere. Quum ergo passiones et vitia, præsertim perfidiæ et delectationes venereæ, mentem obtenebrent, quidam his vitiis sic excæcantur, ut de sua turpitudine non verecundentur, sed potius glorientur, et quasi licitas et honestas reputent delectationes impuras ac sordidas. De quibus scriptum est: Exsultant in rebus pessimis; et in Isaia, Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt.
paras.en: For as concupiscence is twofold, namely carnal and disordered, and spiritual and ordered, as has been said, so pleasure, or the delight that follows it, is twofold. Good and lawful pleasure is the delight joined to a virtuous act: for every virtue has its own delight joined to its working, as it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 21:15|It is joy to the just to do judgment|Gaudium est justo facere justitiam]] [Denis reads *justitiam*, "justice", for *judicium*]. And Aristotle says: The sign of virtue is the delight that arises in the deed. Of this pleasure the Prophet says: [[Ps 91:5|thou hast given me, O Lord, a delight in thy doings|Delectasti me, Domine, in factura tua]]; and: [[Ps 35:9|thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure|Torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos]]. Depraved and vicious pleasure is every delight joined to an unlawful act; of which it is said in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 11:10|youth and pleasure are vain|Adolescentia et voluptas vana sunt]]; and in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:30|Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will|Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluptate tua avertere]] [Denis reads *a voluptate tua*, "from thy pleasure", for *a voluntate tua*, "from thy will"]. Since, then, the passions and vices, especially faithlessness and venereal pleasures, darken the mind, some are so blinded by these vices that they are not ashamed of their foulness but rather glory in it, and reckon impure and filthy pleasures lawful and honourable, as it were. Of them it is written: they [[Prov 2:14|rejoice in the most wicked things|Exsultant in rebus pessimis]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 3:9|they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom|Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt]].

paras.t: Itaque per voluptatem diei intelligitur lucis voluptas. Lux enim significatur appellatione diei, ut quum asserit Paulus: Nos qui diei sumus, sobrii simus. Nam, ut ait Salvator, qui facit veritatem, venit ad lucem.
paras.en: So by *the pleasure of the day* is understood the pleasure of the light. For light is signified by the name of day, as when Paul says: [[1 Thess 5:8|let us, who are of the day, be sober|Nos qui diei sumus, sobrii simus]]. For, as the Saviour says, [[John 3:21|he that doth truth cometh to the light|qui facit veritatem, venit ad lucem]].

paras.t: Deliciis carnalibus et vitiosis affluentes. Tales namque non solum in venereis, sed in suis quoque perfidis documentis, adinventionibusque vanissimis delectantur, in […] suis […] […], juxta vos corporaliter commorando, aut prave agendo, aut vos ad eadem attrahendo pro posse. Oculos habentes plenos adulterii et incessabilis delicti, id est signis et incitamentis adulterationis: quia in oculis lasciviæ mentis præsertim apparet, et per corporalem intuitum provocatur libido. Quæ incessabilis dicitur, quia quo amplius pervagatur seu exercetur, eo plus incitatur et infrenis ac vaga efficitur. Hinc impudicus oculus impudicæ mentis est nuntius. Et in Ecclesiastico habetur: Virginem ne conspicias, ne scandalizeris in decore ejus; noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis; averte faciem tuam a muliere compta; propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt. Idcirco timoratus et sanctus Job dixit: Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis, ne cogitarem quidem de virgine.
paras.en: [[2:13|sporting themselves to excess|Deliciis carnalibus et vitiosis affluentes]] in carnal and vicious delights [the Latin *deliciis affluentes* is literally "abounding in delights"]. For such men take delight not only in venereal things but also in their faithless teachings and most vain inventions; [[2:13|rioting in their feasts with you|in suis]] [some words are lost in the transcription here], by dwelling bodily beside you, or by acting wickedly, or by drawing you to the same things as far as they can. [[2:14|Having eyes full of adultery and of sin that ceaseth not|Oculos habentes plenos adulterii et incessabilis delicti]], that is, full of the signs and incitements of adultery: for the wantonness of the mind shows itself above all in the eyes, and lust is provoked by bodily looking. It is called a sin *that ceaseth not* because the more it roams about or is exercised, the more it is stirred up and becomes unbridled and wandering. Hence the unchaste eye is the messenger of an unchaste mind. And in Ecclesiasticus we have: [[Ecclus 9:5|Gaze not upon a maiden, lest her beauty be a stumblingblock to thee|Virginem ne conspicias, ne scandalizeris in decore ejus]]; [[Ecclus 9:7|Look not round about thee in the ways of the city|noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis]]; [[Ecclus 9:8|Turn away thy face from a woman dressed up|averte faciem tuam a muliere compta]]; [[Ecclus 9:9|many have perished by the beauty of a woman|propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt]]. Therefore holy Job, who feared God, said: [[Job 31:1|I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin|Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis, ne cogitarem quidem de virgine]].

paras.t: Pellicientes animas instabiles. Secundum Bedam, pellices dicuntur meretrices, sumpto vocabulo a pollutione, vel a pellis suæ formositate, qua incautos alliciunt. Pelliciunt ergo animas instabiles, qui homines in fidei veritate et virtutum constantia non bene fundatos pestifere instruunt, ac seducunt. Quocontra loquitur Paulus: Non circumferamur omni vento doctrinæ. Et in Ecclesiastico præcipitur: Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui; et in Proverbiis, Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas illis. Cor exercitatum, id est habituatum, in avaritia habentes, quia assidue cogitant qualiter temporalia sibi accumulent. Quocontra in Ecclesiastico fertur: Nihil iniquius quam amare pecuniam; et: Avaro nihil est scelestius; hic enim animam suam habet venalem. Maledictionis filii, id est maledictione digni: quemadmodum primo Regum David ait ad Abner: Filii mortis estis vos, qui non custodistis dominum vestrum regem, id est morte digni.
paras.en: [[2:14|Alluring unstable souls|Pellicientes animas instabiles]]. According to Bede, harlots are called *pellices*, the word being taken from *pollutio* [defilement], or from the beauty of their *pellis* [skin], with which they entice the unwary [Denis connects *pellicientes*, "alluring", with *pellex*, "harlot"]. Those, then, *allure unstable souls* who give pestilent instruction to men not well grounded in the truth of the faith and in constancy of virtue, and lead them astray. Against which Paul says: Let us not be [[Eph 4:14|carried about with every wind of doctrine|Non circumferamur omni vento doctrinæ]]. And in Ecclesiasticus it is commanded: [[Ecclus 5:12|Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of thy judgment|Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui]]; and in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:10|My son, if sinners shall entice thee, consent not to them|Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas illis]]. [[2:14|having their heart exercised with covetousness|cor exercitatum avaritia habentes]] [*exercitatum*, that is, made a habit], for they think constantly how they may heap up temporal things for themselves. Against which it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|Nihil iniquius quam amare pecuniam]] [the margin gives Eccli. v, 10; the verse is Ecclus 10:10]; and: [[Ecclus 10:9|nothing is more wicked than the covetous man|Avaro nihil est scelestius]]; [[Ecclus 10:10|for such a one setteth even his own soul to sale|hic enim animam suam habet venalem]]. [[2:14|Children of malediction|Maledictionis filii]], that is, worthy of malediction: as in the first book of Kings David says to Abner: [[1 Kings 26:16|you are the sons of death, who have not kept your master|Filii mortis estis vos, qui non custodistis dominum vestrum regem]], that is, worthy of death [the margin gives I Reg. xxvi, 10; the verse is 1 Kings 26:16].

paras.t: Derelinquentes rectam viam, id est divina præcepta, Scripturarum documenta, fidem et legem Christi, exercitia virtuosa, per quæ omnia itur ad Deum, et recto tramite pertingitur ad salutem, erraverunt per vitiorum abrupta, juxta illud Proverbiorum: Relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas. De quibus Vas electionis fatetur: Impii proficient in pejus, errantes et in errorem mittentes. Secuti viam, id est iniquitatem, Balaam ex Bosor, id est ex urbe sic dicta venientem, ut tangit Beda, qui mercedem iniquitatis amavit, quoniam propter munera dedit regi Balac consilium decipiendi filios Israel, juxta illud Numerorum: Pergens ad populum meum, dabo consilium, quod populus tuus faciat populo huic.
paras.en: [[2:15|Leaving the right way|Derelinquentes rectam viam]], that is, the divine commandments, the teachings of the Scriptures, the faith and law of Christ, virtuous exercises, by all of which one goes to God and reaches salvation by a straight path, [[2:15|they have gone astray|erraverunt]] over the precipices of vice, according to that of Proverbs: they [[Prov 2:13|leave the right way, and walk by dark ways|Relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas]]. Of whom the Vessel of election declares: The wicked [[2 Tim 3:13|shall grow worse and worse: erring, and driving into error|proficient in pejus, errantes et in errorem mittentes]]. [[2:15|Having followed the way|Secuti viam]], that is, the iniquity, [[2:15|of Balaam of Bosor|Balaam ex Bosor]], that is, of Balaam coming from the city so called, as Bede touches on, [[2:15|who loved the wages of iniquity|qui mercedem iniquitatis amavit]], since for gifts he gave King Balac counsel on deceiving the children of Israel, according to that of Numbers: [[Num 24:14|going to my people, I will give thee counsel, what this people shall do to thy people|Pergens ad populum meum, dabo consilium, quod populus tuus faciat populo huic]] [Denis's Latin is "what thy people shall do to this people"].

paras.t: Correptionem vero habuit suæ vesaniæ, id est, pro sua insipientissima impietate debite est punitus. Fuit enim occisus a filiis Israel. Correptus quoque fuit ab angelo atque ab asina, ut subditur. Subjugale mutum animal, scilicet asina cui insidebat, loquendi facultatem ex natura sua non habens, voce hominis loquens, prohibuit prophetæ insipientiam. Asina quippe virtute divina insipientiam ipsius Balaam (qui fuit propheta, aliqua ex divina revelatione prænuntiando) redarguit, et eum a cœpto itinere, quantum in se erat, compescuit, dicens: Cur percutis me ecce jam tertio? Quæ omnia in Numerorum libro plenius sunt descripta. Creditur autem quod angelus Dei per os asinæ verba illa formavit, nec asina verba illa intellexit, quum et numerare opus sit rationis, et in verbis illis numeratio fuit, quum dixit, Tertio. Unde, ut asserit Avicenna, gallina numerum pullorum suorum non noscit, sed multitudinem percipit. Dicitur tamen asina reprehendisse Balaam, quoniam verba reprehensoria protulit.
paras.en: [[2:16|But had a check of his madness|Correptionem vero habuit suæ vesaniæ]], that is, he was duly punished for his most foolish impiety: for he was slain by the children of Israel. He was also rebuked by the angel and by the ass, as follows: [[2:16|the dumb beast used to the yoke|Subjugale mutum animal]], namely the ass on which he sat, which by its nature had no power of speech, [[2:16|speaking with man's voice, forbade the folly of the prophet|voce hominis loquens, prohibuit prophetæ insipientiam]]. For the ass, by divine power, reproved the folly of Balaam (who was a prophet, in that he foretold some things by divine revelation) and, as far as lay in her, held him back from the journey he had begun, saying: [[Num 22:28|Why strikest thou me, lo, now this third time?|Cur percutis me ecce jam tertio?]] All of this is described more fully in the book of Numbers. Now it is believed that the angel of God formed those words through the ass's mouth, and that the ass did not understand them, since counting is a work of reason, and there was counting in those words when she said "third". Hence, as Avicenna asserts, a hen does not know the number of her chicks, but perceives a multitude. The ass is nevertheless said to have reproved Balaam, because she uttered words of reproof.

paras.t: Hi sunt fontes sine aqua, id est doctores ficti carentes vera doctrina: quia doctores se esse præsumunt et jactant, quum deceptores existant, sicque assimilantur fonti siccato; et nebulæ turbinibus exagitatæ, id est similes nebulis a ventis hinc inde commotis: quoniam dæmonum suggestionibus et vitiorum impulsibus circumferuntur; quibus caligo tenebrarum reservatur: quia ut ait Salvator, projicientur in tenebras exteriores, ut de tenebris vitiorum præcipitentur in tenebras tormentorum. Et recte obscuritas infernalis caligo tenebrarum, quasi caligo caliginum, appellatur, quum sit vehementissima, quemadmodum rosa flos florum vocatur.
paras.en: [[2:17|These are fountains without water|Hi sunt fontes sine aqua]], that is, pretended teachers lacking true doctrine: for they presume and boast that they are teachers, when they are deceivers, and so they are likened to a dried-up fountain; [[2:17|and clouds tossed with whirlwinds|et nebulæ turbinibus exagitatæ]], that is, like clouds driven this way and that by the winds, since they are carried about by the suggestions of the demons and the impulses of vice; [[2:17|to whom the mist of darkness is reserved|quibus caligo tenebrarum reservatur]]: for, as the Saviour says, they [[Matt 8:12|shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|projicientur in tenebras exteriores]], so that from the darkness of vice they are thrown headlong into the darkness of torments. And the obscurity of hell is rightly called *the mist of darkness*, as it were the darkness of darknesses, since it is most intense, just as the rose is called the flower of flowers.

paras.t: Superba enim vanitatis loquentes, id est verba falsitatis pomposa; vel, ut alii legunt, Superbia vanitatis, id est ex arrogantia propriæ vanitatis, loquentes: pelliciunt in desideriis carnis luxuriæ, id est, per concessionem et approbationem concupiscentiarum carnalium fallunt, eos qui paululum effugiunt, id est imperfectos, qui aliqualiter se ab erroribus ac peccatis cœperunt abstrahere; qui deceptores in errore conversati, id est assuefacti, libertatem illis promittunt, id est, deceptis a se affirmant quod libere sine peccato possint carnalia desideria adimplere. Per quod illos ad talia pronos, faciliter fallunt, quum ipsi hæretici et iniqui, servi sunt corruptionis, id est falsitati ac impietati subjecti. A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est. Ipsi autem a vitiis et a diabolo victi sunt, idcirco vitiorum et dæmonum servi censentur. Propter quod loquitur Paulus: Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur. Et apud Joannem asserit Christus: Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati.
paras.en: [[2:18|For, speaking proud words of vanity|Superba enim vanitatis loquentes]], that is, pompous words of falsehood; or, as others read, *Superbia vanitatis* [that is, "with the pride of vanity"], that is, speaking out of the arrogance of their own vanity, [[2:18|they allure by the desires of fleshly riotousness|pelliciunt in desideriis carnis luxuriæ]], that is, they deceive by allowing and approving carnal lusts, [[2:18|those who for a little while escape|eos qui paululum effugiunt]] [Denis takes *paululum* as "a little", "somewhat"], that is, the imperfect, who have begun in some measure to withdraw themselves from errors and sins; [[2:18|such as converse in error|qui deceptores in errore conversati]] [Denis reads *qui deceptores in errore conversati*, "who, deceivers practised in error", and takes it of the false teachers], that is, accustomed to it, [[2:19|Promising them liberty|libertatem illis promittunt]], that is, they assure those they have deceived that they may freely, without sin, fulfil their carnal desires; and by this they easily deceive those who are inclined to such things, whereas these heretics and wicked men themselves [[2:19|are the slaves of corruption|servi sunt corruptionis]], that is, subject to falsehood and impiety. [[2:19|For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]]. And they have been overcome by vices and by the devil; therefore they are reckoned the slaves of vices and of the demons. For this reason Paul says: [[2 Tim 2:26|they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive|Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur]]. And in John Christ declares: [[John 8:34|whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin|Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati]].

paras.t: Si enim refugientes coinquinationes mundi, id est, mundana et carnalia vitia evitantes, in cognitione, id est per veram fidem et fidelem notitiam, Domini nostri et Salvatoris Jesu Christi, his rursus implicati superantur, id est, recidivando pristinis vitiis involvuntur; facta sunt eis posteriora deteriora prioribus, id est, peccata quæ recidivando et post recidivum commiserunt aut inciderunt, enormiora sunt peccatis ante recidivum commissis, aut per omissionem contractis. Nam vulnera repetita sunt magis periculosa. Et recidivatio ista, propter ingratitudinem sibi annexam, qua quis de priore remissione, illuminatione et gratia Deo ingratus est, et propter præhabitam veritatis notitiam, valde auget et gravat peccata sequentia. Propterea subditur:
paras.en: [[2:20|For if, flying from the pollutions of the world|Si enim refugientes coinquinationes mundi]], that is, shunning worldly and carnal vices, [[2:20|through the knowledge|in cognitione]], that is, through true faith and faithful acquaintance, [[2:20|of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ|Domini nostri et Salvatoris Jesu Christi]], [[2:20|they be again entangled in them and overcome|his rursus implicati superantur]], that is, by relapsing they are wrapped up in their former vices, [[2:20|their latter state is become unto them worse than the former|facta sunt eis posteriora deteriora prioribus]]: that is, the sins they committed or fell into in relapsing and after the relapse are more enormous than the sins committed before the relapse or contracted by omission. For wounds reopened are more dangerous. And this relapse, because of the ingratitude bound up with it, by which a man is ungrateful to God for his earlier forgiveness, enlightenment and grace, and because of the knowledge of the truth he had before, greatly increases and aggravates the sins that follow. Therefore there is added:

paras.t: Melius enim, id est minus malum sive culpabile, erat illis non cognoscere viam justitiæ, id est divina præcepta et ea quæ necessaria sunt saluti, quam post agnitionem retrorsum converti ab eo, quod illis traditum est, sancto mandato, id est ab observantia legis ac fidei christianæ divertere. Nempe quo quis plura a Deo beneficia est sortitus, eo plus obligatus est Deo gratus esse ac deservire. Idcirco doctus gravius peccat quam indoctus, ceteris paribus, præsertim quia qui viam agnoscit justitiæ, nec tamen observat, plus videtur Deum contemnere, quam justitiæ viam ignorans.
paras.en: [[2:21|For it had been better|Melius enim erat]], that is, less evil or blameworthy, [[2:21|for them not to have known the way of justice|illis non cognoscere viam justitiæ]], that is, the divine commandments and the things necessary for salvation, [[2:21|than, after they have known it, to turn back from that holy commandment which was delivered to them|quam post agnitionem retrorsum converti ab eo, quod illis traditum est, sancto mandato]], that is, to turn aside from the keeping of the Christian law and faith. For the more benefits a man has received from God, the more he is bound to be grateful to God and to serve Him. Therefore, other things being equal, the learned man sins more gravely than the unlearned, especially because he who knows the way of justice and yet does not keep it seems to despise God more than one who does not know the way of justice.

paras.t: Propter quod Christus disseruit: Servus qui cognovit voluntatem domini sui, et non fecit, plagis vapulabit multis; qui autem non cognovit, et fecit digna plagis, vapulabit paucis. Hinc dictum est per Jacobum: Scienti bonum facere, et non facienti, peccatum est illi. Imo quam enorme sit istud, constat ex eo quod ad Hebræos legitur: Voluntarie peccantibus nobis post acceptam notitiam veritatis, jam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia. Et rursus ad Hebræos terribiliter loquitur Paulus: Impossibile est eos qui semel sunt illuminati, gustaverunt etiam donum cœleste, et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti, et prolapsi sunt, rursus renovari ad pœnitentiam, rursus crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes. Hinc etiam Veritas contestatur: Si cæci essetis, non haberetis peccatum; nunc autem dicitis, Quia videmus; peccatum vestrum manet.
paras.en: For this reason Christ taught: [[Luke 12:47|that servant, who knew the will of his lord|Servus qui cognovit voluntatem domini sui]] [[Luke 12:47|and did not|et non fecit]], [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]]; [[Luke 12:48|But he that knew not and did things worthy of stripes shall be beaten with few stripes|qui autem non cognovit, et fecit digna plagis, vapulabit paucis]]. Hence it was said by James: [[Jas 4:17|To him therefore who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti bonum facere, et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]. Indeed, how enormous this is appears from what we read to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:26|if we sin wilfully after having the knowledge of the truth, there is now left no sacrifice for sins|Voluntarie peccantibus nobis post acceptam notitiam veritatis, jam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia]]. And again Paul speaks terribly to the Hebrews: [[Heb 6:4|it is impossible for those who were once illuminated, have tasted also the heavenly gift and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost|Impossibile est eos qui semel sunt illuminati, gustaverunt etiam donum cœleste, et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti]], [[Heb 6:6|And are fallen away: to be renewed again to penance, crucifying again to themselves the Son of God and making him a mockery|et prolapsi sunt, rursus renovari ad pœnitentiam, rursus crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes]]. Hence the Truth also bears witness: [[John 9:41|If you were blind, you should not have sin: but now you say: We see. Your sin remaineth|Si cæci essetis, non haberetis peccatum; nunc autem dicitis, Quia videmus; peccatum vestrum manet]].

paras.t: Sed si ista ita se habent, videtur ignorantia hominem excusare. Imo apparet quod quum homo sit fragilis, tutius sit non discere neque agnoscere viam justitiæ, quam eam cognoscere, ne forte post ejus cognitionem contingat peccare, et graviorem reatum incurrere. Respondetur, quod ignorantia juris quod quis scire tenetur, non excusat a culpa, nec ignorantia crassa, seu affectata; sed ignorantia facti, adhibita diligentia bona, ignorantia quoque invincibilis, prorsus excusant. Et quamvis malum sit post veritatis notitiam cadere, ipsa tamen notitia in se bona est et optanda, et frequenter a variis malis præservat, et confert ad hoc ut homo resurgat celerius. Porro, qui viam nescit justitiæ, sine retinaculo errat, nec surgit.
paras.en: But if these things are so, it seems that ignorance excuses a man; indeed it appears that, since man is frail, it is safer not to learn or know the way of justice than to know it, lest perhaps after knowing it one should happen to sin and incur a graver guilt. The answer is that ignorance of the law which one is bound to know does not excuse from fault, nor does crass or affected ignorance [that is, ignorance due to gross neglect, or chosen deliberately so as to sin more freely]; but ignorance of fact, when good diligence has been used, and invincible ignorance too, excuse entirely. And though it is an evil to fall after knowing the truth, yet the knowledge itself is good in itself and to be desired; it often preserves a man from various evils and helps him to rise again more quickly. Whereas he who does not know the way of justice wanders without a check, and does not rise.

paras.t: Cur autem enormius sit post justitiæ agnitionem peccare, subjungitur. Contingit enim illis, scilicet recidivantibus, id veri proverbii. Idcirco ait, Veri proverbii, quia quod sequitur, ex libro Proverbiorum Salomonis acceptum est. Canis reversus ad suum vomitum. Sic siquidem Salomon in Proverbiis loquitur: Sicut canis qui revertitur ad vomitum suum, ita stultus qui iterat stultitiam suam. Nam, sicut id quod per vomitum est ejectum, resumere est valde abominabile, fœtens ac turpe; sic peccata pœnitendo deleta reiterare. Quod vero adjungitur, Sus lota in volutabro luti, princeps Apostolorum de suo apposuit, valdeque apte: nam sicut ex tali lotione efficitur porca sordidior quam fuerat ante, ita ex recidivo gravius homo coinquinatur. Itaque sicut vomens superfluam ejicit materiam qua premebatur: sic peccator confitendo effundit mentis venenum quod animam pressit; dum vero post pœnitentiam recidivat, instar canis redit ad vomitum, id est, quod salubriter evomuit, damnabiliter repetit. Postremo, in Scripturis per stultum designatur quicumque in mortali est vitio, et per stultitiam omnis mortalis intelligitur culpa. Sic in Ecclesiaste asseritur: Stultorum infinitus est numerus.
paras.en: Why it is more enormous to sin after knowing justice is then added: [[2:22|For, that of the true proverb|id veri proverbii]] [[2:22|has happened to them|Contingit enim illis]], namely to those who relapse.
