He says *of the true proverb* because what follows is taken from the book of the Proverbs of Solomon: [[2:22|The dog is returned to his vomit|Canis reversus ad suum vomitum]]. For thus Solomon speaks in Proverbs: [[Prov 26:11|As a dog that returneth to his vomit, so is the fool that repeateth his folly|Sicut canis qui revertitur ad vomitum suum, ita stultus qui iterat stultitiam suam]]. For as it is most abominable, stinking and foul to take up again what has been cast out by vomiting, so is it to repeat sins blotted out by penance. But what is added, [[2:22|The sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire|Sus lota in volutabro luti]], the Prince of the Apostles put in of his own, and very aptly: for as by such a washing the sow is made filthier than she was before, so by relapse a man is more gravely defiled. And so, as one who vomits throws out the superfluous matter that oppressed him, so the sinner by confessing pours out the poison of the mind that weighed on his soul; but when after penance he relapses, he returns like the dog to his vomit, that is, he takes up again to his damnation what he had cast out to his health. Lastly, in the Scriptures *the fool* means anyone who is in mortal sin, and by *folly* every mortal fault is understood. So it is said in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 1:15|the number of fools is infinite|Stultorum infinitus est numerus]].

3.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI TERTII : HANC ECCE VOBIS, CARISSIMI, SECUNDAM SCRIBO EPISTOLAM.
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: Behold this second epistle I write to you, my dearly beloved.

paras.t: Hoc ultimo capitulo gloriosissimus apostolici chori hierarcha plenius destruit hæreticas pravitates, et fideles in fide confortat.
paras.en: In this last chapter the most glorious hierarch of the apostolic choir destroys the wicked errors of the heretics more fully, and strengthens the faithful in the faith.

paras.t: Hanc ecce vobis, carissimi, secundam scribo epistolam, in quibus prima et secunda epistolis, vestram excito in commonitione, id est per hanc caritativam exhortationem, sinceram mentem a vitiis expurgatam, ut memores sitis memoria virtuosis actionibus juncta, eorum quæ prædixi, verborum Prophetarum et Apostolorum sanctorum, id est verborum a sanctis Prophetis Apostolisque prolatorum, videlicet documentorum ac mandatorum quæ tradiderunt. Aliqui textus habent, Verborum a Prophetis, et redit in idem : nam sensus est, Verborum dictorum a Prophetis. Memores quoque estote præceptorum Domini et Salvatoris nostri, id est præceptorum quæ Christus Dominus et Salvator in Evangelio dedit, qui decem præceptis aliqua addidit. Hæc memoria ad exsecutionem operis est ordinanda, juxta illud in Psalmo : Memores sunt mandatorum ipsius ad faciendum ea.
paras.en: [[3:1|Behold this second epistle I write to you, my dearly beloved|Hanc ecce vobis, carissimi, secundam scribo epistolam]], [[3:1|in which|in quibus]], that is, in the first and second epistles, [[3:1|I stir up by way of admonition|vestram excito in commonitione]], that is, by this loving exhortation, [[3:1|your sincere mind|sinceram mentem]], cleansed of vices, [[3:2|That you may be mindful|ut memores sitis]], with a remembrance joined to virtuous deeds, [[3:2|of those words which I told you before|eorum quæ prædixi, verborum]] [[3:2|from the holy prophet and of your apostles|Prophetarum et Apostolorum sanctorum]] [Denis's text reads "of the words of the holy Prophets and Apostles"], that is, of the words uttered by the holy Prophets and Apostles, namely of the teachings and commandments which they handed down. Some texts have "of the words from the Prophets", and it comes to the same: for the sense is, "of the words spoken by the Prophets". Be mindful also [[3:2|of the precepts of the Lord and Saviour|præceptorum Domini et Salvatoris nostri]], that is, of the precepts which Christ, the Lord and Saviour, gave in the Gospel, who added some things to the ten commandments. This remembrance is to be directed to the carrying out of the work, according to that in the Psalm, of those who [[Ps 102:18|are mindful of his commandments to do them|Memores sunt mandatorum ipsius ad faciendum ea]].

paras.t: Hoc primum scientes, inter ea quæ jam scienda commemoro, quod venient in novissimis diebus, præsertim circa Antichristi adventum, in deceptione, id est ad introducendum deceptionem, illusores Scripturarum ac fidei christianæ atque fidelium, juxta proprias concupiscentias ambulantes, id est vitiose carnaliterque viventes; et dicentes : Ubi est promissio aut adventus ejus? id est, ubi manent, aut quando apparebunt et implebuntur, quæ Jesus Nazarenus promisit suis cultoribus? Et quando ad judicium veniet ipse, prout prædixit? tanquam dicant : Omnia vana sunt et conficta, nec erit judicium, nec resurrectio mortuorum. Ex quo enim patres nostri dormierunt, omnia sic perseverant ab initio creaturæ : id est, ab exordio sæculi et generationis humanæ, et a temporibus antiquissimis, in quibus obierunt progenitores nostri primævi, mundus juxta solitum cursum naturæ processit, duravit, nec notabiliter est mutatus : ergo nec in futuro mutabitur, nec generationum cessabit successio. Quemadmodum ergo Paulus secunda ad Thessalonicenses redarguit eos qui tunc secundum adventum Christi de proximo imminere asseruerunt, Non terreamini, inquiens, quasi instet dies Domini; sic princeps Apostolorum nunc eos condemnat qui de nimia dilatione secundi adventus Domini causabantur. Præinductis demum sanctissimi Petri verbis consonant, quæ ad Timotheum scripta sunt, ubi Vas electionis fatetur : In novissimis diebus instabunt tempora periculosa, et erunt homines amantes se ipsos, etc.
paras.en: [[3:3|Knowing this first|Hoc primum scientes]], among the things which I now recall as needing to be known, [[3:3|That in the last days there shall come|quod venient in novissimis diebus]], especially about the coming of Antichrist, [[3:3|deceitful|in deceptione]], that is, to bring in deception, [[3:3|scoffers|illusores]] at the Scriptures and at the Christian faith and at the faithful, [[3:3|walking after their own lusts|juxta proprias concupiscentias ambulantes]], that is, living viciously and carnally; [[3:4|Saying: Where is his promise or his coming?|dicentes : Ubi est promissio aut adventus ejus?]] That is: where are they, or when will they appear and be fulfilled, the things which Jesus of Nazareth promised to his worshippers? And when will he himself come to judgment, as he foretold? As though they said: "All these things are empty and made up; there will be neither judgment nor resurrection of the dead." [[3:4|For since the time that the fathers|Ex quo enim patres]] (our fathers) [[3:4|slept|dormierunt]], [[3:4|all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation|omnia sic perseverant ab initio creaturæ]]: that is, from the beginning of the world and of the human race, and from the most ancient times, in which our first forefathers died, the world has gone on according to the usual course of nature, has lasted, and has not been noticeably changed: therefore neither will it be changed in the future, nor will the succession of generations cease. So, then, as Paul in the second epistle to the Thessalonians rebukes those who then asserted that the second coming of Christ was close at hand, saying, [[2 Thess 2:2|nor be terrified|Non terreamini]], [[2 Thess 2:2|as if the day of the Lord were at hand|quasi instet dies Domini]], so the prince of the Apostles now condemns those who made complaint of the too long delay of the Lord's second coming. Lastly, with these words of most holy Peter set out above there agrees what was written to Timothy, where the Vessel of election declares: [[2 Tim 3:1|in the last days shall come dangerous times|In novissimis diebus instabunt tempora periculosa]], and [[2 Tim 3:2|Men shall be lovers of themselves|erunt homines amantes se ipsos]], etc.

paras.t: Consequenter probat summus Apostolus falsum esse quod illi dicent, omnia a principio creaturæ sic perseverare. Latet enim eos hoc volentes, id est, qui illud dicturi sunt, nesciunt, quod cœli erant prius, et terra de aqua et per aquam consistens Dei verbo : per quæ ille tunc mundus inundatus periit. Oportet advertere, quod beatissimus Petrus non loquitur hic de superioribus cœlis, supra sphæram actionis et passionis subsistentibus, qui ex sua natura sunt incorruptibiles quantum ad suum esse substantiale, sed loquitur de cœlis aeriis, id est partibus aeris superioris et inferioris. Unde per Jeremiam Dominus loquitur : Milvus in cœlo cognovit tempus suum. Et quarto Regum asseritur : Ascendit Elias per turbinem in cœlum. Hinc etiam aves cœli vocantur, quia in aere volant. Porro, quod de his cœlis solummodo jam loquatur sacratissimus Petrus, hinc constat, quia intendit probare quod mundus semel per diluvium periit, et rursus in fine igne peribit. Idcirco non loquitur nisi de cœlis quos attigit aqua, et ignis attinget. Certumque est quod aqua sphæram lunæ non attigit, nec ignis conflagrationis creditur altius ascensurus quam ipsa ascenderat aqua. Et istud Thomas super quartum affirmat Sententiarum. Beda quoque, Albertus, et alii expositores concordant in isto.
paras.en: Next the supreme Apostle proves that what they will say is false, namely that all things continue so from the beginning of the creation. [[3:5|For this they are wilfully ignorant of|Latet enim eos hoc volentes]], that is, those who are to say it do not know, [[3:5|That the heavens were before|quod cœli erant prius]], [[3:5|and the earth out of water and through water, consisting by the word of God|et terra de aqua et per aquam consistens Dei verbo]]: [[3:6|Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished|per quæ ille tunc mundus inundatus periit]]. We must notice that most blessed Peter is not speaking here of the higher heavens, which stand above the sphere of action and passion [that is, above the region of the elements, where bodies act upon one another and are changed], and which by their nature are incorruptible as to their substantial being; but he is speaking of the aerial heavens, that is, of the parts of the upper and lower air. Hence the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 8:7|The kite in the air hath known her time|Milvus in cœlo cognovit tempus suum]] [the Latin says "in the heaven": the Douay-Rheims renders it "in the air"]. And it is said in the fourth book of Kings: [[4 Kings 2:11|Elias went up by a whirlwind into heaven|Ascendit Elias per turbinem in cœlum]]. Hence too birds are called birds of the heaven, because they fly in the air. Moreover, that most sacred Peter is here speaking only of these heavens is clear from this, that he means to prove that the world once perished by the flood[[Gen 7:17||]] [the margin gives Gen. vii, 17–24], and will perish again at the end by fire. Therefore he speaks only of the heavens which the water reached and the fire will reach. And it is certain that the water did not reach the sphere of the moon, nor is the fire of the conflagration believed to be going to rise higher than the water itself had risen. And Thomas affirms this on the fourth book of the Sentences. Bede too, Albert, and other expositors agree in this.

paras.t: Est igitur sensus : Cœli erant prius, id est, ab exordio ante diluvium fuerunt cœli aerii, quantum ad suam substantiam, ut pote inferior pars aeris, et pars ejus superior quæ est supra cacumina montium, quam superiorem aeris partem aqua diluvii occupavit, quoniam quindecim cubitis altior fuit altissimis montibus terræ, ut scribitur in Genesi. Et terra etiam prius, scilicet ante diluvium, fuit de aqua, id est, per separationem aquarum a superficie terræ apparuit terra, juxta illud Genesis : Congregentur aquæ in locum unum, et appareat arida, et factum est ita. Et hæc eadem terra est per aquam consistens Dei verbo, id est ex omnipotentis Dei decreto sive præcepto terra sui […] consistit, et permanet in esse per hoc, quod partibus ejus undique supra superficiem ejus, et intra viscera ejus aqua miscetur, ut partes terræ sibi cohæreant : aliter redigerentur in pulverem. Propter quod asserit Avicenna : Ex terra pura non fit lapis, quia requiritur aqua, per quam fit continuatio partium terræ. Hinc loquitur Beda : Divina dispositione venis aquarum terra tota intrinsecus plena est, quemadmodum corpus animalium sanguinis venis repletur, ne ariditate terra deficiat, si aquarum cesset rigatio. Videmus namque æstatis calore terras consumpto earum humore flaccentes, atque in pulverem quem projicit ventus, esse redactas. Per quæ, hoc est per cœlos præfatos aerios et per terram, ille tunc mundus inundatus, id est inferior regio mundialis aquis perfusa, operta et occupata, periit, quantum ad viva contenta in terra et aere, præter ea quæ erant in arca. Nam omnia mortua tunc fuerunt. Periit etiam ille mundus, videlicet terra, aqua et aer, scilicet regio illa elementaris, quantum ad multa. Nam pristinum fructificandi vigorem perdidit terra, atque in variis locis ac partibus aliam dispositionem accepit. Sed et magna pars aeris corrumpebatur et vertebatur in aquas. Tunc quoque rupti sunt omnes fontes abyssi magnæ, puta Oceani.
paras.en: The sense, then, is this: [[3:5|the heavens were before|Cœli erant prius]], that is, from the beginning, before the flood, there were the aerial heavens as to their substance, namely the lower part of the air and its upper part, which is above the tops of the mountains; and this upper part of the air the water of the flood took up, since it was fifteen cubits higher than the highest mountains of the earth, as is written in Genesis[[Gen 7:20||]]. [[3:5|and the earth|Et terra]] too was before, that is, before the flood, [[3:5|out of water|de aqua]], that is, the earth appeared through the separating of the waters from the face of the earth, according to that of Genesis: [[Gen 1:9|Let the waters|Congregentur aquæ]] [[Gen 1:9|be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done|in locum unum, et appareat arida, et factum est ita]]. And this same earth is [[3:5|through water, consisting by the word of God|per aquam consistens Dei verbo]], that is, by the decree or command of almighty God the earth […] consists and remains in being through this, that water is mingled with its parts on every side, above its surface and within its bowels, so that the parts of the earth hold together: otherwise they would be reduced to dust. For this reason Avicenna asserts: "Stone is not made from pure earth, since water is required, through which the parts of the earth are made continuous." Hence Bede says: "By God's disposition the whole earth is full within of veins of water, as the body of animals is filled with veins of blood, lest the earth fail through dryness if the watering of the waters should cease. For we see that in the heat of summer, when their moisture is used up, lands grow slack and are reduced to dust, which the wind drives away." [[3:6|Whereby|Per quæ]], that is, by the aforesaid aerial heavens and by the earth, [[3:6|the world that then was, being overflowed with water|ille tunc mundus inundatus]], that is, the lower region of the world, drenched, covered and taken up by the waters, [[3:6|perished|periit]], as to the living things contained in the earth and air, except those that were in the ark. For all these died then. That world also perished, namely earth, water and air, that is, that region of the elements, in many respects. For the earth lost its former vigour of bearing fruit, and in various places and parts it received another disposition. And a great part of the air too was corrupted and turned into waters. Then also [[Gen 7:11|all the fountains of the great deep were broken up|rupti sunt omnes fontes abyssi magnæ]], namely of the Ocean.

paras.t: Cœli autem qui nunc sunt, id est prætacti cœli aerii, et terra quæ nunc est, id est, jam in rerum natura subsistunt, eodem verbo repositi sunt, id est, ex divino præcepto ad convenientem naturalemque formam et statum quos nunc habent, reducti sunt, per hoc quod aquæ diluvii cessaverunt, et terra et ignis ad pristinum statum ac modum, quantum ad multa, tunc redierunt. Servati sunt in diem judicii et perditionis iniquorum hominum, id est, igne conflagrationis sunt exurendi atque purgandi in die judicii, qui est dies perditionis seu condemnationis hominum iniquorum. De quo die scriptum est : In diem perditionis servabitur malus et ad diem furoris ducetur; et de furore Omnipotentis bibet. In Proverbiis quoque : Omnia propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus, impium quoque ad diem malum.
paras.en: [[3:7|But the heavens|Cœli autem]] [[3:7|which are now|qui nunc sunt]], that is, the aerial heavens spoken of above, [[3:7|and the earth|et terra]] which is now, that is, which now exist in the nature of things, [[3:7|by the same word are kept in store|eodem verbo repositi sunt]], that is, by God's command they have been brought back to the fitting and natural form and state which they now have, in that the waters of the flood ceased, and the earth and the fire then returned, in many respects, to their former state and manner. They are [[3:7|reserved|Servati sunt]] [[3:7|against the day of judgment and perdition of the ungodly men|in diem judicii et perditionis iniquorum hominum]], that is, they are to be burnt and purged by the fire of the conflagration on the day of judgment, which is the day of the perdition or condemnation of wicked men. Of which day it is written: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servabitur malus et ad diem furoris ducetur]]; and [[Job 21:20|he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty|et de furore Omnipotentis bibet]] [the margin gives only Job xxi, 30; these last words are from Job 21:20]. In the Proverbs also: [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself: the wicked also for the evil day|Omnia propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus, impium quoque ad diem malum]].

paras.t: Consequenter princeps Apostolorum breviter probat, quod propter dilationem futuri judicii æstimare nequaquam debemus futurum non esse judicium illud, quum omnis dilatio ista sit modica in Dei conspectu, et comparatione perpetuæ durationis eam sequentis. Nam subditur : Unum vero hoc non lateat vos, carissimi ; et quid sit hoc unum, subjungit : quia unus dies apud Dominum sicut mille anni, et mille anni sicut dies unus : id est, spatium quod Deus comparatione suæ æternitatis atque futuræ retributionis reputat quasi unum diem, est sicut mille anni, id est spatium multo longissimum secundum nostram computationem ac apparentiam ; et mille anni apud nos, id est spatia temporum quantumlibet diuturna, sunt coram Deo quasi dies unus, quia suæ æternitatis respectu quasi momentum est. Propter quod ait Psalmista : Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos, tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit. Vel sensus verborum istorum est, quod supersapientissimus Deus omnia in suæ æternitatis nunc seu momento conspiciens, ita contemplatur unum diem ut mille annos, et mille annos ut diem unum, quoniam cuncta præterita, præsentia et futura invariabiliter intuetur.
paras.en: Next the prince of the Apostles briefly proves that because of the delay of the judgment to come we ought by no means to think that that judgment will not come, since all this delay is small in God's sight, and in comparison with the everlasting duration that follows it. For he adds: [[3:8|But of this one thing be not ignorant, my beloved|Unum vero hoc non lateat vos, carissimi]]; and what this one thing is, he goes on to say: [[3:8|that one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day|quia unus dies apud Dominum sicut mille anni, et mille anni sicut dies unus]]: that is, the space which God, in comparison with his eternity and with the retribution to come, reckons as one day, is as a thousand years, that is, a very long space indeed by our reckoning and to our appearance; and a thousand years with us, that is, spaces of time however long, are before God as one day, since in respect of his eternity it is as a moment. Wherefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 89:4|For a thousand years in thy sight are as yesterday, which is past|Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos, tanquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit]]. Or the sense of these words is that God, who is wise beyond all wisdom, beholding all things in the now or moment of his eternity [the single, unchanging "now" of eternity, in which all times are present to God], so looks upon one day as a thousand years and a thousand years as one day, since he beholds unchangeably all things past, present and to come.

paras.t: Porro, ut Beda refert, quidam prætacta verba sic intelligenda putarunt, quasi dies judicii per mille annos sit duraturus, non attendentes quod non simpliciter ait, Erit unus dies sicut mille anni, sed, Unus dies apud Dominum ut mille anni. Si autem dicere vellet quod dies judicii mille annorum spatio tenderetur, non opus fuisset ponere, Apud Dominum, quoniam dies illa etiam apud homines tantæ longitudinis esset.
paras.en: Further, as Bede relates, some thought the aforesaid words were to be understood as though the day of judgment were to last for a thousand years, not observing that he does not say simply, "There shall be one day as a thousand years", but, [[3:8|one day with the Lord is as a thousand years|Unus dies apud Dominum ut mille anni]]. But if he had meant to say that the day of judgment would stretch over a space of a thousand years, there would have been no need to put [[3:8|with the Lord|Apud Dominum]], since that day would be of such length among men too.

paras.t: Vult ergo beatissimus Petrus insinuare, quod omnium dierum et annorum finem certissime noscat Deus, certissime quoque prænoverit quando adventus sit adimplendus, et quando promissa præmia sint Sanctis reddenda. Idcirco subjungitur : Non tardat Dominus promissum, id est, promissa sua implere non differt ultra tempus præfixum ac debitum. Sic et in Habacuc habetur : Apparebit Dominus in finem, et non mentietur ; si moram fecerit, exspecta eum, quia veniens veniet, et non tardabit. Sed patienter agit, id est, longanimiter præstolatur, et differt judicium, propter vos, id est propter melius vestrum, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti. Sic et Christus testatur : Non est voluntas ante Patrem ut pereat unus ex his pusillis. Et ad Timotheum asseritur : Deus omnes homines vult salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire. In Ezechiele quoque habetur : Numquid voluntatis meæ est mors impii, dicit Dominus, et non ut convertatur a viis suis, et vivat?
paras.en: Most blessed Peter means, then, to suggest that God knows most surely the end of all days and years, and also foreknows most surely when the coming is to be accomplished, and when the promised rewards are to be rendered to the Saints. Therefore it is added: [[3:9|The Lord delayeth not his promise|Non tardat Dominus promissum]], that is, he does not put off fulfilling his promises beyond the time fixed and due. So too it is found in Habacuc: The Lord [[Hab 2:3|shall appear at the end, and shall not lie: if it make any delay, wait for it: for it shall surely come, and it shall not be slack|Apparebit Dominus in finem, et non mentietur ; si moram fecerit, exspecta eum, quia veniens veniet, et non tardabit]] [Denis's text has "the Lord shall appear"; the Douay-Rheims, speaking of the vision, "it shall appear"]. [[3:9|but dealeth patiently|Sed patienter agit]], that is, waits long-sufferingly and puts off the judgment, [[3:9|for your sake|propter vos]], that is, for your greater good, [[3:9|not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]]. So also Christ bears witness: [[Matt 18:14|it is not the will of your Father|Non est voluntas ante Patrem]] [[Matt 18:14|that one of these little ones should perish|ut pereat unus ex his pusillis]]. And it is asserted to Timothy: God [[1 Tim 2:4|will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|omnes homines vult salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire]]. In Ezechiel also we find: [[Ezech 18:23|Is it my will that a sinner should die, saith the Lord God, and not that he should be converted from his ways, and live?|Numquid voluntatis meæ est mors impii, dicit Dominus, et non ut convertatur a viis suis, et vivat?]]

paras.t: Sed quomodo possunt hæc stare, quum per Isaiam Deus testetur, Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet? Quum enim Dei voluntas omnipotens sit, utique adimplebitur. Propter quod in libro Esther legitur : Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita, et non est qui tuæ resistere possit voluntati. Denique si tanta est felicitas civium supernorum, ut quidquid velint, præsto sit eis : quanto magis superbeatissimi Dei infinita exigit beatitudo, ut nil divinæ voluntati contrarium possit accidere? — Ad hæc duplex est responsio : Prima, quod Deus quantum in se est, non vult quemquam perire, sed omnes salvari. Nam omnes ad pœnitentiam ac salutem hortatur, et pœnitentibus semper paratus est indulgere, nec alicui quod in se est facienti, denegat gratiam, imo per angelos sanctos custodit ac dirigit homines ; nec ex parte Dei est defectus salutis cujuscumque pereuntis, quum Deus variis modis homines ad meliora invitet. Secunda responsio est, quod Deus non vult quemquam perire, sed omnes salvari : loquendo de voluntate antecedente, hoc est, considerando homines secundum quod homines sunt, utpote rationalis naturæ, felicitatis capaces, non autem loquendo de voluntate consequente, utpote considerando eos ut tales aut tales : quemadmodum rex terrenus vult omnes subditos suos prosperari ac vivere, in quantum sunt subditi sui, non autem in quantum quidam eorum malefici sunt, et rebelles, fures, homicidæ, latrones.
paras.en: But how can these things stand, when God testifies through Isaias, [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]? For since God's will is almighty, it will surely be fulfilled. For this reason we read in the book of Esther: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power, and there is none that can resist thy will|Domine, Rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita, et non est qui tuæ resistere possit voluntati]]. Lastly, if the happiness of the citizens on high is so great that whatever they wish is at hand for them, how much more does the infinite beatitude of the more-than-most-blessed God require that nothing contrary to the divine will can happen? To this there is a twofold answer. The first, that God, as far as lies in him, wills no one to perish, but all to be saved. For he exhorts all to penance and salvation, and is always ready to pardon the penitent, and denies grace to no one who does what lies in him; nay, he guards and guides men through the holy angels; and the failure of salvation in anyone who perishes does not come from God's side, since God invites men to better things in many ways. The second answer is that God wills no one to perish, but all to be saved, speaking of his antecedent will, that is, considering men as they are men, namely of a rational nature and capable of happiness; but not speaking of his consequent will, namely considering them as such or such [antecedent will: God's will regarding man as such, before the circumstances of each; consequent will: his will regarding each as he in fact is]: just as an earthly king wills all his subjects to prosper and live, in so far as they are his subjects, but not in so far as some of them are evildoers and rebels, thieves, murderers, robbers.

paras.t: Insuper, ut recitat Beda, qui dixerunt diem judicii per mille annos duraturum, ideo hoc dixerunt, quia putabant n[…] ut electi qui in fine mundi in peccatis aliquibus morientur, intra spatium […]tum purgentur : non attendentes q[…] sit impudentiæ dicere, quod ceteri universi electi et justi suis corporibus […] oculi ictu resumptis, per tot annos in terra aut aere præstolabuntur finem judicii, atque a præparata ac debita eis beatitudine differentur. — Quod quum […] sit, quam sacrilegum et mendosum […] quod sceleratissimus asserit Mahometus […] scriptis suis, diem judicii per quinquaginta millium annorum spatium duraturum.
paras.en: Moreover, as Bede recounts, those who said that the day of judgment would last for a thousand years said this because they thought […] that the elect who die at the end of the world in some sins should be purged within […] space: not considering […] impudence it is to say that all the other elect and just, having taken back their bodies […] in the twinkling of an eye, will wait for so many years on earth or in the air for the end of the judgment, and will be kept back from the beatitude prepared for them and due to them. And since this is […], how sacrilegious and lying […] what the most wicked Mahomet asserts […] his writings, that the day of judgment will last for a space of fifty thousand years.

paras.t: Itaque Deus differt judicii diem, t[…]terim compleatur numerus electorum […] homines per pœnitentiam se expurgent : quemadmodum ad Hebræos scribitur : Juxta fidem defuncti sunt omnes isti […] acceptis repromissionibus, Deo melius aliquid providente de nobis, ut non […] nobis consummarentur. Unde ut in Apocalypsi inducitur, animabus martyrum […] ultionis optantibus, respondetur divinitus ut requiescant tempus adhuc modicum donec compleatur numerus conservorum eorum.
paras.en: And so God puts off the day of judgment […] meanwhile the number of the elect may be filled up […] men may cleanse themselves by penance: as is written to the Hebrews: [[Heb 11:13|All these died according to faith|Juxta fidem defuncti sunt omnes isti]] […] [[Heb 11:13|having received the promises|acceptis repromissionibus]], [[Heb 11:40|God providing some better thing for us|Deo melius aliquid providente de nobis]], that they should not be perfected […] us [the margin gives Hebr. xi, 14; the words are from Heb 11:13 and 11:40]. Hence, as is set forth in the Apocalypse, when the souls of the martyrs long for […] of vengeance[[Apoc 6:10||]], answer is made from God [[Apoc 6:11|that they should rest for a little time|ut requiescant tempus adhuc modicum]], until the number of their fellow servants be filled up.

paras.t: Adveniet autem dies Domini, id est […] judicii, qui specialiter dicitur dies Domini seu Christi judicis summi, qui est Dominus sabbati et temporis universi. Dies, inquam, judicii specialiter dicitur […] Domini, quia in eo ipse præcipue […] omnipotentiam, sapientiam, justitiam declarabit, suam operationem efficiet, […] voluntatem complebit. Tanquam fur, […] est repente et improvise, Paulo testante : Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus ; et rursus, Dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet. Ideo ait Salvator : De die illa et hora nemo scit ; et in Actibus, Non est vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate. In quo cœli magno impetu transient, id est, cœli aerii, de quibus jam locutus est, grandi impulsu per ignem conflagrationis alterabuntur, atque a statu quem nunc habent, deficient. Aliquæ etiam partes aeris illo igne tunc corrumpentur. Denique aer terræ proximus, in Scripturis interdum vocatur cœlum, quum in Job dicatur : Amici Job sparserunt pulverem super capita sua in cœlum. Elementa vero calore ignis, quo conflagrabitur et purgabitur mundus inferior, solventur eo modo quo cœli tunc transibunt. Elementa namque transibunt et solventur : Primo, quoad cessationem motus et operationis eorum, quia non movebuntur ut modo, nec erit in eis generatio sive corruptio. Secundo, quantum ad mutuam transmutationem, quia per qualitates suas contrarias non alterabunt se invicem, nec in se mutuo agent ut nunc : quia cessante primi mobilis motu, cessabunt ista in inferioribus. Tertio, quantum ad innovationem, quia tunc transferentur ad dispositionem nobiliorem, et claritatem mirificam sortientur : quia ut creditur, terra splendebit ut aurum, aqua sicut crystallus, aer ut cœlum, ignis ut astra.
paras.en: [[3:10|But the day of the Lord shall come|Adveniet autem dies Domini]], that is, […] of judgment, which is called in a special way the day of the Lord, or of Christ the supreme judge, who is Lord of the sabbath[[Matt 12:8||]] [the margin gives only Matth. xii] and of all time. The day of judgment, I say, is called in a special way […] of the Lord, because in it he will above all make known […] almighty power, wisdom and justice, will carry out his work, and will fulfil […] will. [[3:10|as a thief|Tanquam fur]], […] is suddenly and without warning, as Paul testifies: [[1 Thess 5:3|when they shall say: Peace and security; then shall sudden destruction come upon them|Quum dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus]]; and again, [[1 Thess 5:2|the day of the Lord shall so come as a thief in the night|Dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet]]. Therefore the Saviour says: [[Matt 24:36|of that day and hour no one knoweth|De die illa et hora nemo scit]]; and in the Acts: [[Acts 1:7|It is not for you to know the time or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power|Non est vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta quæ Pater posuit in sua potestate]]. [[3:10|in which the heavens shall pass away with great violence|In quo cœli magno impetu transient]], that is, the aerial heavens of which he has already spoken will be altered with a great shock by the fire of the conflagration, and will fall away from the state which they now have. Some parts of the air too will then be corrupted by that fire. Lastly, the air next to the earth is sometimes called heaven in the Scriptures, since it is said in Job: Job's friends [[Job 2:12|sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven|sparserunt pulverem super capita sua in cœlum]]. [[3:10|and the elements|Elementa vero]] [[3:10|shall be melted|solventur]] [[3:10|with heat|calore]] of the fire by which the lower world will be burnt up and purged, in the same way in which the heavens will then pass away. For the elements will pass away and be melted: first, as to the ceasing of their motion and working, since they will not be moved as now, nor will there be generation or corruption in them. Secondly, as to their changing into one another, since they will not alter one another by their contrary qualities, nor act upon one another as now: for when the motion of the first moving heaven [the primum mobile, the outermost moving sphere, whose motion drives all the others] ceases, these things will cease in the lower bodies. Thirdly, as to renewal, since they will then be brought to a nobler disposition and will receive a wonderful brightness: for, as is believed, the earth will shine like gold, the water like crystal, the air like the heaven, the fire like the stars.

paras.t: […] ra, exurentur : quia non solum terra igne purgabitur, partimque caloris vehementia consumetur, sed et plantæ, ac bruta, ac cetera mixta, secundum se tota corruptibilia, penitus corrumpentur. Elementa vero, quia secundum se tota corruptibilia non sunt, secundum substantiam et modo præfato manebunt, præsertim quum sint de integritate consistentiæ ac ordinis universi : quamvis Beda videatur aliter hic sentire. Nam ait : Quatuor sunt elementa, quibus mundus iste consistit, ignis, aer, aqua, et terra : quæ cuncta ignis maximus ille absumet. Nec cuncta in tantum consumet ut funditus non sint, sed duo in totum consumet, duo vero in meliorem restituet faciem. Duo autem quæ dicit penitus consumenda, sunt ignis et aqua. Augustinus quoque in libro de Civitate Dei, relinquit sub dubio de aqua, quum in Apocalypsi legatur : Mare jam non est. Sed doctores scholastici asserunt, elementa omnia secundum substantiam permansura, præsertim quum ignis et aqua nobiliora sint terra. Porro quod dicitur, Mare jam non est, intelligitur sicut et illud : Cœlum et terra transibunt.
paras.en: […] [[3:10|and the earth and the works which are in it shall be burnt up|exurentur]]: for not only will the earth be purged by fire, and partly consumed by the violence of the heat, but also plants and beasts and the other mixed bodies [that is, bodies compounded of the elements], which are corruptible as wholes, will be utterly corrupted. But the elements, since they are not corruptible as wholes, will remain as to their substance, and in the manner described above, especially since they belong to the completeness of the make-up and order of the universe: although Bede seems to think otherwise here. For he says: "There are four elements of which this world consists, fire, air, water and earth: all of which that greatest fire will take away. Nor will it so consume them all that they are utterly no more; but two it will consume entirely, and two it will restore to a better face." And the two which he says are to be wholly consumed are fire and water. Augustine too, in the book of the City of God, leaves the water in doubt, since we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:1|the sea is now no more|Mare jam non est]]. But the scholastic doctors assert that all the elements will remain as to their substance, especially since fire and water are nobler than earth. Further, what is said, "the sea is now no more", is understood as that other saying is: [[Matt 24:35|Heaven and earth shall pass|Cœlum et terra transibunt]].

paras.t: Quum ergo hæc omnia jam prædicta solvenda sint, id est corrumpenda seu alteranda, vel immutanda, juxta sensum præhabitum, quales, id est, quam diligentes, assiduos, et constantes, oportet vos esse in sanctis conversationibus, id est virtuosis operibus ? præsertim in operibus misericordiæ, tam corporalibus quam spiritualibus, de quibus specialiter fiet judicium, ut in Matthæo habetur. Ideo additur, et pietatibus : quod etiam potest exponi de duplici pietate, utpote de ea quæ est virtus moralis, et subvenit proximo in quantum est indigens, et ea quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, et subvenit proximo in quantum ad Dei imaginem et similitudinem est creatus, ut quidam distinguunt. Expectantes districtum Dei judicium, et properantes in adventum, id est, celeriter ac ferventer vos præparantes ad secundum adventum, qui erit in fine : adventum, inquam, [diei] Domini nostri Jesu Christi, per quem, id est cujus imperio ac virtute, cœli ardentes, id est cœli aerii igne calefacti, solventur, secundum sensum inductum, et elementa, videlicet aqua et terra, ignis ardore tabescent, id est, a suo statu et modo deficient, partimque desinent, sicut expositum est.
paras.en: [[3:11|Seeing then that all these things|Quum ergo hæc omnia]] already foretold [[3:11|are to be dissolved|solvenda sint]], that is, are to be corrupted, or altered, or changed, according to the sense given above, [[3:11|what manner of people|quales]], that is, how diligent, earnest and steadfast, [[3:11|ought you to be in holy conversation|oportet vos esse in sanctis conversationibus]], that is, in virtuous works? Especially in the works of mercy, corporal as well as spiritual, on which in particular the judgment will be made, as is found in Matthew[[Matt 25:34||]]. Therefore it is added, [[3:11|and godliness|et pietatibus]] [pietas, "godliness" or "piety"]: which can also be explained of a twofold piety, namely of that which is a moral virtue and helps our neighbour in so far as he is in need, and of that which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]] and helps our neighbour in so far as he is created to the image and likeness of God, as some distinguish them. [[3:12|Looking for|Expectantes]] the strict judgment of God, [[3:12|and hasting unto the coming|et properantes in adventum]], that is, quickly and fervently preparing yourselves for the second coming, which will be at the end: the coming, I say, [[3:12|of the day|diei]] of our Lord Jesus Christ, [[3:12|by which|per quem]], that is, by whose command and power, [[3:12|the heavens being on fire|cœli ardentes]], that is, the aerial heavens heated by fire, [[3:12|shall be dissolved|solventur]] in the sense set out above, [[3:12|and the elements|et elementa]], namely water and earth, [[3:12|shall melt with the burning heat|ignis ardore tabescent]], that is, will fall away from their state and manner, and partly cease, as has been explained.

paras.t: Quasi diceret : Valde virtuosos, timoratos, exemplares oportet vos esse, consideratione rigoris divini judicii. Si enim tam horribilia signa illud præcedent, et si tantam horribilitatem ac districtionem omnipotens, justus, metuendus Creator in rebus inanimatis monstrabit, certum est quod illud judicium in se ipso incomparabiliter ineffabiliterque durissimum erit. Et in ipsis hominibus impiis ineffabilem Deus ostendet severitatem, tanto certe majorem, quanto nunc clementius diuturniusque exspectat. Propter quod sanctus Job loquitur : Quis mihi hoc tribuat, ut in inferno protegas me et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei ? Et Psalmista : Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus, justitia et judicium correctio sedis ejus ; ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus. Apud Isaiam quoque fertur : Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo, ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum ; labia ejus repleta sunt indignatione ; spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans ad perdendas gentes.
paras.en: As if he said: You ought to be very virtuous, God-fearing and exemplary, considering the rigour of the divine judgment. For if such dreadful signs go before it, and if the almighty, just and fearsome Creator shows such dreadfulness and strictness in inanimate things, it is certain that that judgment in itself will be incomparably and unspeakably hard. And upon wicked men themselves God will show an unspeakable severity, greater indeed by as much as he now waits more mercifully and longer. Wherefore holy Job says: [[Job 14:13|Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass, and appoint me a time when thou wilt remember me?|Quis mihi hoc tribuat, ut in inferno protegas me et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei ?]] And the Psalmist: [[Ps 96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne|Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus, justitia et judicium correctio sedis ejus]]; [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about|ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus]]. In Isaias too it is said: [[Is 30:27|Behold the name of the Lord cometh from afar, his wrath burneth, and is heavy to bear: his lips are filled with indignation|Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo, ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum ; labia ejus repleta sunt indignatione]]; [[Is 30:28|His breath as a torrent overflowing|spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans]] [[Is 30:28|to destroy the nations|ad perdendas gentes]].

paras.t: Novos vero cælos et novam terram, et promissa ipsius exspectamus. Non ait, Alios cœlos et aliam terram, sed, Novos, id est quantum ad modum et proprietates innovatos ac meliores effectos, et similiter terram novam et meliorem effectam. Cetera quoque Dei promissa, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, dotesque corporum glorificatorum et animarum felicium, præstolamur : quia et ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei, ut dicitur ad Romanos octavo. Hinc apud Isaiam Dominus contestatur : Ecce ego creo cœlos novos et terram novam. In Apocalypsi quoque ait Joannes : Vidi cœlum novum et terram novam ; et dixit qui sedebat in throno : Ecce nova facio omnia. In quibus justitia habitat, id est habitabit, ut sit sermo propheticus, de futuro per modum præsentis, propter certitudinem prophetiæ, loquens. Tunc enim in corporeis illis cœlis ac terra, divina præclarissime relucebit justitia, universis tunc tribuens quod promeruerunt, et electorum gloriam augens in cœlorum ac elementorum innovatione, in quorum inspectione gaudebunt. Habitabit etiam in illis justitia : quia ut in Apocalypsi habetur, non intrabit in civitatem cœlestem ac patriam Beatorum aliquid coinquinatum, sed soli justi, in quibus nunquam injustitia locum poterit obtinere, quia confirmati erunt in bono ; et erunt tunc omnia ad justitiæ æqualitatem plene redacta.
paras.en: [[3:13|But we look for new heavens and a new earth|Novos vero cælos et novam terram]], [[3:13|according to his promises|et promissa ipsius exspectamus]] [Denis's text reads "and we look for his promises"]. He does not say, "other heavens and another earth", but "new", that is, renewed as to their manner and properties and made better, and likewise a new earth, made better. We wait also for the other promises of God, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt]], and for the endowments of glorified bodies [the dotes, the gifts of the risen body: impassibility, brightness, agility and subtlety] and of blessed souls: for [[Rom 8:21|the creature also itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption, into the liberty of the glory of the children of God|et ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei]], as is said in the eighth chapter to the Romans. Hence the Lord declares in Isaias: [[Is 65:17|behold I create new heavens, and a new earth|Ecce ego creo cœlos novos et terram novam]]. In the Apocalypse also John says: [[Apoc 21:1|I saw a new heaven and a new earth|Vidi cœlum novum et terram novam]]; and [[Apoc 21:5|he that sat on the throne, said: Behold, I make all things new|dixit qui sedebat in throno : Ecce nova facio omnia]]. [[3:13|in which justice dwelleth|In quibus justitia habitat]], that is, will dwell, so that it is prophetic speech, speaking of the future in the manner of the present because of the certainty of the prophecy. For then in those bodily heavens and earth the divine justice will shine out most brightly, giving to all then what they have deserved, and increasing the glory of the elect in the renewal of the heavens and of the elements, in the sight of which they will rejoice. Justice will also dwell in them because, as is found in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 21:27|There shall not enter|non intrabit]] into the heavenly city and fatherland of the Blessed [[Apoc 21:27|any thing defiled|aliquid coinquinatum]], but only the just, in whom injustice will never be able to find a place, since they will be confirmed in good; and all things will then be fully brought to the evenness of justice.

paras.t: Ex quibus infertur salubris monitio, dum subditur : Propter quod, carissimi, hæc exspectantes, satagite immaculati et inviolati, id est mente et corpore purificati, fide et opere integri, a mortalibus et venialibus vitiis emundati, ei inveniri, id est ad Dei honorem ac gloriam veraciter apparere [in pace]. Tanta enim felicitas omni diligentia et labore est dignissima, nec Deus cernetur nisi a purgatissimis mentibus. Propter quod loquitur Judæis : Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Et ad Hebræos dicitur : Pacem sequimini et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit. Hanc sententiam introduxit Vas electionis secunda ad Corinthios : Has, inquiens, habentes promissiones, mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Domini. Itaque, Beati immaculati in via, qui ambulant in lege Domini ; beatus vir cui non imputavit Dominus peccatum. Hinc ait Salvator : Beati servi illi, quos, quum venerit Dominus, invenerit vigilantes.
paras.en: From these things a wholesome warning is drawn, as he adds: [[3:14|Wherefore, dearly beloved, waiting for these things, be diligent|Propter quod, carissimi, hæc exspectantes, satagite]] [[3:14|unspotted and blameless|immaculati et inviolati]], that is, purified in mind and body, whole in faith and in work, cleansed of mortal and venial faults, [[3:14|that you may be found before him|ei inveniri]], that is, to appear truly to the honour and glory of God, [[3:14|in peace|in pace]]. For so great a happiness is most worthy of all diligence and labour, and God will not be seen except by the most purified minds. Wherefore he [that is, Christ] says to the Jews: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. And it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace|Pacem sequimini]] [[Heb 12:14|and holiness: without which no man shall see God|et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit]]. The Vessel of election brought in this thought in the second epistle to the Corinthians, saying: [[2 Cor 7:1|Having therefore these promises|habentes promissiones]], [[2 Cor 7:1|let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God|mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Domini]]. And so, [[Ps 118:1|Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord|Beati immaculati in via, qui ambulant in lege Domini]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxiii, 1; the words are Ps 118:1]; [[Ps 31:2|Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin|beatus vir cui non imputavit Dominus peccatum]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 12:37|Blessed are those servants whom the Lord, when he cometh, shall find watching|Beati servi illi, quos, quum venerit Dominus, invenerit vigilantes]].

paras.t: Et Domini nostri Jesu Christi longanimitatem, id est diuturnam seu piam præstolationem, ac dilationem suæ remunerationis, salutem arbitramini, id est, salutarem vobis esse sentite : quia confert vobis ad gloriæ incrementum, ut et interim quotidie proficiatis, et plures salventur. Sicut et carissimus frater noster Paulus secundum datam sibi sapientiam, id est ei infusam in raptu suo usque ad tertium cœlum, quando vidit Deum per speciem, secundum Augustinum, et audivit verba arcana quæ non licet homini loqui, scripsit vobis. Quod enim scripsit uni Ecclesiæ, omnibus scripsit, quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio ait : Quod vobis (vel uni) dico, omnibus dico. Et quia beatissimus Petrus ambas suas scripsit epistolas electis advenis dispersionis Ponti, Galatiæ, Asiæ, etc., videtur quod eisdem scripsit et Paulus, qui Galatis Asianisque scripsit, ut certum est : quod et verba sequentia videtur prætendere. Nam subditur :
paras.en: And account [[3:15|the longsuffering of our Lord|Et Domini nostri Jesu Christi longanimitatem]] Jesus Christ, that is, his long or loving waiting, and the putting off of his reward, [[3:15|salvation|salutem arbitramini]], that is, hold it to be salutary for you: since it serves to increase your glory, so that both you may meanwhile advance daily, and more may be saved. [[3:15|as also our most dear brother Paul, according to the wisdom given him|Sicut et carissimus frater noster Paulus secundum datam sibi sapientiam]], that is, infused into him in his rapture [[2 Cor 12:2|to the third heaven|usque ad tertium cœlum]], when he saw God by sight [per speciem: by direct vision of God's essence, not through a likeness], according to Augustine, and [[2 Cor 12:4|heard secret words which it is not granted to man to utter|audivit verba arcana quæ non licet homini loqui]], [[3:15|hath written to you|scripsit vobis]]. For what he wrote to one Church he wrote to all, as Christ says in the Gospel: [[Mark 13:37|what I say to you|Quod vobis]] (or, to one) [[Mark 13:37|I say to all|dico, omnibus dico]]. And since most blessed Peter wrote both his epistles [[1 Pet 1:1|to the strangers dispersed through Pontus|electis advenis dispersionis Ponti]], Galatia, Asia, etc., it seems that Paul too wrote to the same people, since he wrote to the Galatians and to the Asians, as is certain: which the following words also seem to show. For it is added:

paras.t: Sicut et in omnibus epistolis, id est, ceteris universis, loquens in eis de his de quibus ego jam scripsi vobis, utpote primo et secundo Christi adventu, innovationeque mundi, moralibus documentis, salutaribusque præceptis, et de vitandis hæreticis, de patientia quoque et constantia ad martyrium ; in quibus Pauli epistolis sunt quædam difficilia intellectu, id est ad intelligendum : quia in singulis ejus epistolis sunt talia multa, ea quæ Philemoni scripta est exempta. Præsertim in epistola ad Romanos, aliquot locos reperias quovis labyrintho magis extricatu difficiles. Quæ indocti et instabiles, præsertim hæretici, depravant, id est, false exponunt, male intelligunt, pervertunt, corrumpunt, addendo, subtrahendo, seu aliis modis, sicut et ceteras Scripturas, ad suam ipsorum perditionem, id est ad propriam condemnationem gravissimam : quia non Paulo, sed sibi ipsis enormiter nocuerunt sic faciendo. Qui recte indocti vocantur, quoniam veris atque catholicis caruerunt doctrinis. Et erant instabiles, quoniam suis erroribus, vitiis et passionibus undique fluctuabant, nec in Deo, nec in ratione, nec in virtutibus fixi. De quibus ait Propheta : In circuitu impii ambulant ; et, Impii tanquam pulvis ante faciem venti. Unde in Proverbiis fertur : Quasi tempestas transiens, impius non erit ; justus autem, quasi fundamentum æternum.
paras.en: [[3:16|As also in all his epistles|Sicut et in omnibus epistolis]], that is, in all the rest, [[3:16|speaking in them of these things|loquens in eis de his]] of which I have already written to you, namely of the first and second coming of Christ, and the renewal of the world, of moral teachings and wholesome precepts, and of the avoiding of heretics, of patience also and steadfastness unto martyrdom; [[3:16|in which|in quibus]] epistles of Paul [[3:16|are certain things hard to be understood|sunt quædam difficilia intellectu]], that is, hard to understand: for in each of his epistles there are many such things, except the one written to Philemon. Especially in the epistle to the Romans you will find some places harder to disentangle than any labyrinth. [[3:16|which the unlearned and unstable|Quæ indocti et instabiles]], especially the heretics, [[3:16|wrest|depravant]], that is, falsely expound, misunderstand, pervert, corrupt, by adding, by taking away, or in other ways, [[3:16|as they do also the other scriptures, to their own destruction|sicut et ceteras Scripturas, ad suam ipsorum perditionem]], that is, to their own most grievous condemnation: for by doing so they did great harm, not to Paul, but to themselves. They are rightly called unlearned, because they lacked true and Catholic teaching. And they were unstable, because they were tossed about on every side by their errors, vices and passions, fixed neither in God, nor in reason, nor in the virtues. Of whom the Prophet says: [[Ps 11:9|The wicked walk round about|In circuitu impii ambulant]]; and, The wicked are [[Ps 1:4|like the dust|tanquam pulvis]] before the face of the wind. Hence it is said in the Proverbs: [[Prov 10:25|As a tempest that passeth, so the wicked shall be no more: but the just is as an everlasting foundation|Quasi tempestas transiens, impius non erit ; justus autem, quasi fundamentum æternum]].

paras.t: Denique beatissimus et sapientissimus princeps Apostolorum, epistolas Pauli specialiter commendat et approbat: tum, quia tam Judæi obstinati quam hæretici specialiter detraxerunt Paulo, et epistolis ejus ; secundo, quoniam Paulus diffusius ac difficilius scripsit, idcirco de suarum depravatione epistolarum majus fuit periculum. Præterea, in his resplendet profundissima gloriosissimi archiapostoli Petri humilitas, qui Paulum tam excellenter collaudat, quum Paulus in sua ad Galatas epistola reprehenderit Petrum : quod eum non latuit. Sancti etenim viri non proprias quærunt aut diligunt laudes, sed veritatis præconia, virtutum sublimia, justitiæ zelum, Dei honorem, animarum salutem: propriam quoque reprehensionem beneficium arbitrantur præcipuum. Non enim ad se ipsos reflectuntur inordinate, sed in Deum firmiter sunt conversi.
paras.en: Lastly, the most blessed and most wise prince of the Apostles especially commends and approves the epistles of Paul: first, because both the obstinate Jews and the heretics especially disparaged Paul and his epistles; secondly, because Paul wrote at greater length and with more difficulty, and so there was greater danger of his epistles being wrested. Moreover, in these words there shines out the most profound humility of the most glorious archapostle Peter, who praises Paul so excellently, though Paul in his epistle to the Galatians had reproved Peter[[Gal 2:11||]]: which was not unknown to him. For holy men do not seek or love their own praises, but the proclaiming of truth, the heights of the virtues, zeal for justice, the honour of God, the salvation of souls; and they count a reproof of themselves an especial benefit. For they do not turn back upon themselves inordinately, but are firmly turned towards God.

paras.t: Deinde finalis exhortatio subinfertur. Vos ergo, fratres, præscientes Christum judicem esse venturum, hæreticos quoque diversa falsitatum portenta esse docturos, custodite, id est, ea quæ scripsi, memoriter retinete, et opere adimplete : juxta illud Psalmi, In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Quod autem aliqui libri habent, Vosmetipsos, non est de essentia veri textus, sed additum. Ne insipientium errore traducti, id est hæreticorum aut aliorum pravis doctrinis infecti, atque extra veritatis limites ad falsa translati, excidatis a propria firmitate, id est, a fidei ac virtutum constantia deficiatis. Hinc ad Thessalonicenses loquitur Paulus : Ne quis vos seducat ullo modo; itemque : Stabiles, inquit, et immobiles estote, abundantes in opere Domini semper. Unde et Christus hortatur : Videte ne quis vos seducat : surgent enim pseudoprophetæ et pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna et prodigia, ita ut in errorem inducantur (si fieri potest) etiam electi.
paras.en: Then the final exhortation is added. [[3:17|You therefore, brethren, knowing these things before|Vos ergo, fratres, præscientes]], that is, knowing beforehand that Christ will come as judge, and that heretics too will teach various monstrous falsehoods, [[3:17|take heed|custodite]], that is, keep in memory what I have written, and fulfil it in deed: according to that of the Psalm, [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. As for some books having "yourselves" [custodite vosmetipsos, "keep yourselves"], that does not belong to the true text, but has been added. [[3:17|lest being led aside by the error of the unwise|Ne insipientium errore traducti]], that is, infected by the wicked teachings of heretics or others, and carried beyond the bounds of truth to falsehoods, [[3:17|you fall from your own steadfastness|excidatis a propria firmitate]], that is, fall away from constancy in faith and in the virtues. Hence Paul says to the Thessalonians: [[2 Thess 2:3|Let no man deceive you by any means|Ne quis vos seducat ullo modo]]; and again: [[1 Cor 15:58|be ye steadfast|Stabiles]], he says, [[1 Cor 15:58|and unmoveable: always abounding in the work of the Lord|et immobiles estote, abundantes in opere Domini semper]]. Hence Christ too exhorts: [[Matt 24:4|Take heed that no man seduce you|Videte ne quis vos seducat]]: [[Matt 24:24|there shall arise false Christs and false prophets and shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch as to deceive (if possible) even the elect|surgent enim pseudoprophetæ et pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna et prodigia, ita ut in errorem inducantur (si fieri potest) etiam electi]].

paras.t: Crescite vero in gratia, bene agendo, viriliter laborando, mentem assidue custodiendo, proficite in omni virtute, ac dono Spiritus Sancti, præsertim quum non crescere sit decrescere, et cognitione Domini nostri et Salvatoris Jesu Christi, id est in formata ipsius notitia, et in contemplatione suæ divinitatis sincera, in intelligentia mysteriorum ipsius, et in omnibus quæ sacra Scriptura docet de eo. In quorum cognitione proficit homo, legendo, ab aliis audiendo, per se diligenter considerando, præsertim divinam illuminationem suscipiendo, in dono sapientiæ donoque intellectus proficiendo, angelicam instructionem sumendo. Hinc ad Colossenses loquitur S. Paulus : Postulamus ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis Dei, in omni sapientia et intellectu spirituali, per omnia crescentes in scientia Dei. Ad Philippenses quoque : Existimo omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Per Osee quoque ait Deus : Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta. Siquidem hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscamus Patrem verum Deum, et quem misit Jesum Christum. Ipsi gloria, id est majestas, beatitudo, lætitia, et clara cum laude fama, et nunc et in diem æternitatis, id est in militanti et triumphanti Ecclesia, in præsenti et in futuro, in via ac patria, qui cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto unus est Deus super omnia sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[3:18|But grow in grace|Crescite vero in gratia]]: by doing well, by labouring manfully, by guarding the mind constantly, advance in every virtue and gift of the Holy Ghost, especially since not to grow is to go back; [[3:18|and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ|et cognitione Domini nostri et Salvatoris Jesu Christi]], that is, in a formed knowledge of him [that is, a knowledge given life by charity, as formed faith is], and in a pure contemplation of his Godhead, in understanding of his mysteries, and in all that holy Scripture teaches about him. In the knowledge of these things a man advances by reading, by hearing from others, by careful thought of his own, above all by receiving the divine light, by advancing in the gift of wisdom and the gift of understanding, and by taking instruction from the angels. Hence St. Paul says to the Colossians: We [[Col 1:9|beg that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding|Postulamus ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis Dei, in omni sapientia et intellectu spirituali]], in all things [[Col 1:10|increasing in the knowledge of God|crescentes in scientia Dei]]. To the Philippians also: [[Phil 3:8|I count all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|Existimo omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Through Osee too God says: [[Osee 6:6|the knowledge of God more than holocausts|Scientiam Dei volo plus quam holocausta]]. For [[John 17:3|this is eternal life|hæc est vita æterna]], [[John 17:3|That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|ut cognoscamus Patrem verum Deum, et quem misit Jesum Christum]] [Denis's wording: "that we may know the Father, the true God, and Jesus Christ whom he sent"]. [[3:18|To him be glory|Ipsi gloria]], that is, majesty, beatitude, joy, and bright renown with praise, [[3:18|both now and unto the day of eternity|et nunc et in diem æternitatis]], that is, in the Church militant and triumphant, in the present and in the future, on the way and in the fatherland: who with the Father and the Holy Ghost is one God, exalted above all things and blessed. Amen.
